Every news organization that operates in that region, that operates in China, you just have to be really, really careful and thoughtful about it, but you can’t let it compromise the reporting.Do you feel like it compromises the reporting here in the United States?No. I think that global news organizations actually — and if you think about The New York Times, which has reporters in Tehran — have thought really hard about this. There are stories that you have your correspondent in Washington write that you wouldn’t have somebody on the ground in Tehran write. And obviously, we think a lot about the safety of our reporters, but it’s a complicated question.I asked that question because I see what the Trump administration does to journalists here.It’s funny, because I think that we obviously are in this, as you said, free speech crisis here in all sorts of ways. I don’t think it’s like a monarchy that doesn’t have the First Amendment. I think we’re a long way from that.To me, the closer parallel to the Gulf is personalist rule. People talk a lot about corruption, but when you think about these relationships, often it’s a totally different style of doing business where you’re helping your friends and family. But it’s like a totally different modality that obviously in the American tradition is incredibly corrupt. In other parts of the world, that’s just the nature of business. I think that’s how parts of the Trump administration operate.The Trump family in particular sees that as a model. That was the comparison I was making. You can see them enriching themselves, particularly in that part of the world.I do think that elements of that style of doing business are more like other parts of the world. Obviously a lot of the speech stuff here is terrible, but it’s really not like… I mean, just as somebody who operates there, it’s not like being in a country without the First Amendment.Fair enough. Lastly, I just want to talk about AI in your newsroom for one second. We’ve talked a lot about AI in the industry. You make a lot of stuff. The pull, especially when you go make a bunch of video, is to fire ever more content into these algorithms. We haven’t really talked about it. Maybe the only journalistic ethics crisis I’ve never brought to you is, how should we use AI?Because I know that you’re such a purist. It’s funny, I go back and forth on how high impact it will be, but right now I’m like all the way forth on this. A colleague of mine built this great internal tool that is too boring to explain, but it’s going to totally change all of our lives internally. And I’m now a huge believer in the SaaSpocalypse. It’s all going away.You cancel your Trello contract and you’re done.Some of this internal tooling is amazing. We also produced this report out of Semafor World Economy where it was a five-day event with three simultaneous stages and 300 interviews.On Saturday morning, I texted the team, “Hey, I know you’re all tired, but could everybody write a little like ‘what I learned at Semafor World Economy’?” And everyone said, “Ugh.” And then Reed Albergotti, our great tech editor, said, “Give me a couple of hours.” He dropped all the transcripts into Codex or Cowork and then produced something that said, “Here are the most commonly made statements. Here are some disagreements.”We then spent a week hammering through that and actually wound up creating a lot more work for humans. But the notion of, “What’s the takeaway from these 300 conversations?” That’s a job for AI basically. It’s a very hard thing, because no one was in all of them. They were simultaneous.That was a great product that we then released and will continue to build on. I’m actually very bullish about AI, but fundamentally the best parts of reporting are gathering new information that isn’t on the internet and then communicating it with people. Everything in between is production and is very vulnerable to AI. Those things I think are pretty defensible.It’s a good argument. I’m going to come around to it, I promise. I’m going to come around to it. This very much was a conversation exactly like the conversation we have over beers all the time.Okay. I have an AI question for you.There’s a tool that allows you, on a podcast — if you screwed something up, if you’ve mispronounced somebody’s name — to drop it in with your own voice so you don’t have to go back into the studio and rerecord that sentence. Is that okay or not? This is an argument we’re having internally.It depends on exactly how misleading you think you’re going to be.No, just like you mispronounced my name in the intro, and your producer said, “Hey, can you come back into the studio?” It’s Saturday morning.So if I mispronounced your name to you on air?No, in your intro.No, because then that’s just an edit. I would just pick it up.No, I know, but you have to go into the studio and rerecord that. But you’re on a boat doing whatever it is you do. And your producer can just take your voice and redo it.That’s fine. I honestly think that’s fine.I think that’s fine too. Okay, good.The deception comes if I mispronounce your name to you here, and then you leave, and then I make it better. If I’ve done something misleading. If I’m just picking up audio that you would have never heard and we’re just going to do an edit, we’re editing that anyway.Okay, good. I feel the same way.To me, the line always comes down to who is being deceived. And if you’re literally going to deceive the guest and you’re going to create a moment that never happened, probably you’re way over the line.Although honestly, that’s a standard practice in television. They’ll recut the questions.I’ve heard this. Although, now they’re all getting in trouble and I have to publish the full transcript, or the Trump administration sues them.Ben, this has been great. Like I said, this is very much like many of the conversations we’ve had in private. I hope the audience can feel it. Thank you so much.I really enjoyed it. I love the show, and thank you for having me on.Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!Decoder with Nilay PatelA podcast from The Verge about big ideas and other problems.SUBSCRIBE NOW!Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.Nilay Patel

blocks.html_en: Today I’m talking to Ben Smith, the editor-in-chief of Semafor.

sentences.en: Today I’m talking to Ben Smith, the editor-in-chief of Semafor.
sentences.zh: 今天我要采访的是 Semafor 的主编 Ben Smith。

blocks.html_en: Everywhere you go, people say they don’t trust the media — and yet they’ve never consumed more of it. Audiences have moved on from legacy names in favor of Substacks and podcasts and TikTok news influencers that seem to be everywhere in our feeds.

sentences.en: Everywhere you go, people say they don’t trust the media — and yet they’ve never consumed more of it.
sentences.zh: 无论你走到哪里，人们都会说他们不信任媒体——但他们对媒体的了解却从未如此之多。

sentences.en: Audiences have moved on from legacy names in favor of Substacks and podcasts and TikTok news influencers that seem to be everywhere in our feeds.
sentences.zh: 受众已经从传统名称转向 Substacks、播客和 TikTok 新闻影响者，这些在我们的提要中似乎无处不在。

blocks.html_en: Why would anyone want to start a new global news organization in the middle of all that, when even once-storied brands like CBS News can’t seem to figure it out?

sentences.en: Why would anyone want to start a new global news organization in the middle of all that, when even once-storied brands like CBS News can’t seem to figure it out?
sentences.zh: 为什么有人想在这一切之中建立一个新的全球新闻机构，即使是像哥伦比亚广播公司新闻这样的曾经的传奇品牌似乎也无法弄清楚这一点？

blocks.html_en: Well, that’s what Ben did four years ago. He’s the guy who ran BuzzFeed News at the height of the Facebook traffic boom, and even wrote a book about it, called Traffic, which he discussed with me on Decoder back in 2023.

sentences.en: Well, that’s what Ben did four years ago.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是本四年前所做的。

sentences.en: He’s the guy who ran BuzzFeed News at the height of the Facebook traffic boom, and even wrote a book about it, called Traffic, which he discussed with me on Decoder back in 2023.
sentences.zh: 他是在 Facebook 流量繁荣时期运营 BuzzFeed News 的人，甚至还写了一本关于 BuzzFeed News 的书，名为《Traffic》，早在 2023 年他就在 Decoder 上与我讨论过这本书。

blocks.html_en: Around that same time, he cofounded Semafor, which launched in 2022 with a stated goal of reaching 200 million college-educated readers.

sentences.en: Around that same time, he cofounded Semafor, which launched in 2022 with a stated goal of reaching 200 million college-educated readers.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，他与​​他人共同创立了 Semafor，该网站于 2022 年推出，其既定目标是覆盖 2 亿受过大学教育的读者。

blocks.html_en: You’re going to hear Ben say that since then, Semafor has evolved into what he calls an anti-scale company. It still doesn’t have a website paywall, but it makes about half its money in the convening business — that’s what media types have taken to calling events lately.

sentences.en: You’re going to hear Ben say that since then, Semafor has evolved into what he calls an anti-scale company.
sentences.zh: 你会听到 Ben 说，从那时起，Semafor 已经发展成为他所说的一家反规模公司。

sentences.en: It still doesn’t have a website paywall, but it makes about half its money in the convening business — that’s what media types have taken to calling events lately.
sentences.zh: 它仍然没有网站付费专区，但它大约有一半的收入来自召集业务——这就是媒体类型最近在召集活动上采取的做法。

blocks.html_en: And Semafor throws some big events. It actually has a new one called Silicon Valley & The World, which will feature some of the biggest names in tech and AI. That’s part of the events business: hosting the subjects you cover on your big event stage.

sentences.en: And Semafor throws some big events.
sentences.zh: Semafor 举办了一些大型活动。

sentences.en: It actually has a new one called Silicon Valley & The World, which will feature some of the biggest names in tech and AI.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它有一个名为“硅谷与世界”的新项目，其中将包括一些科技和人工智能领域的知名人士。

sentences.en: That’s part of the events business: hosting the subjects you cover on your big event stage.
sentences.zh: 这是活动业务的一部分：在大型活动舞台上举办您涵盖的主题。

blocks.html_en: So I wanted to know how that all works, and what it feels like to navigate the ethical conflicts that seem to be everywhere in media right now. In particular, I wanted to dig into how Semafor’s newsroom is approaching AI, the ethics and optics of putting people you cover on your conference advisory boards, and whether independence is still something an audience is willing to pay for.

sentences.en: So I wanted to know how that all works, and what it feels like to navigate the ethical conflicts that seem to be everywhere in media right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我想知道这一切是如何运作的，以及应对目前媒体中似乎无处不在的道德冲突是什么感觉。

sentences.en: In particular, I wanted to dig into how Semafor’s newsroom is approaching AI, the ethics and optics of putting people you cover on your conference advisory boards, and whether independence is still something an audience is willing to pay for.
sentences.zh: 我特别想深入了解 Semafor 的新闻编辑室如何对待人工智能、将您报道的人员纳入会议顾问委员会的道德和观点，以及观众是否仍然愿意为独立性付费。

blocks.html_en: Ben and I usually hash this stuff out over beers, and I think you can tell we really enjoy getting into all this together.

sentences.en: Ben and I usually hash this stuff out over beers, and I think you can tell we really enjoy getting into all this together.
sentences.zh: 本和我通常会一边喝啤酒一边讨论这些问题，我想你可以看出我们真的很喜欢一起讨论这一切。

blocks.html_en: Okay: Semafor editor-in-chief Ben Smith. Here we go.

sentences.en: Okay: Semafor editor-in-chief Ben Smith.
sentences.zh: 好的：Semafor 主编 Ben Smith。

sentences.en: Here we go.
sentences.zh: 开始了。

sentences.en: This transcript has been lightly edited for length and clarity.
sentences.zh: 为了篇幅和清晰度，本文字记录经过了轻微编辑。

blocks.html_en: Ben Smith, you’re the co-founder and editor in chief of Semafor. Welcome back to Decoder.

sentences.en: Ben Smith, you’re the co-founder and editor in chief of Semafor.
sentences.zh: Ben Smith，您是 Semafor 的联合创始人兼主编。

sentences.en: Welcome back to Decoder.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到解码器。

blocks.html_en: It is really nice to be back.

sentences.en: It is really nice to be back.
sentences.zh: 回来真是太好了。

blocks.html_en: I’m excited to talk to you. You were on the show three years ago, just as Semafor was launching. It was right as Buzzfeed News, which you founded and ran for a long time, was shutting down.

sentences.en: I’m excited to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能和你说话。

sentences.en: You were on the show three years ago, just as Semafor was launching.
sentences.zh: 三年前，当 Semafor 推出时，您就参加了这个节目。

sentences.en: It was right as Buzzfeed News, which you founded and ran for a long time, was shutting down.
sentences.zh: 恰逢您创立并经营了很长时间的 Buzzfeed News 即将关闭。

blocks.html_en: I keep talking to media CEOs about what is going to happen. It feels like you have figured something out at Semafor. How are things going over there?

sentences.en: I keep talking to media CEOs about what is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我一直在与媒体首席执行官谈论即将发生的事情。

sentences.en: It feels like you have figured something out at Semafor.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像你在 Semafor 找到了一些东西。

sentences.en: How are things going over there?
sentences.zh: 那边情况怎么样？

blocks.html_en: Things are going incredibly well, and knock on wood as I say that, but I think we figured something out. There are a lot of different things to figure out, and we’re in this unbelievably strange and unstable moment in media.

sentences.en: Things are going incredibly well, and knock on wood as I say that, but I think we figured something out.
sentences.zh: 事情进展得非常顺利，正如我所说的那样，但我认为我们已经找到了一些办法。

sentences.en: There are a lot of different things to figure out, and we’re in this unbelievably strange and unstable moment in media.
sentences.zh: 有很多不同的事情需要弄清楚，我们正处于媒体这个令人难以置信的奇怪和不稳定的时刻。

blocks.html_en: But I do think we’ve figured out a model that is quality journalism built around great journalists, paired with really large scale convening that is building both great journalism and a really good business, a profitable business — which is something that is, to me as a former BuzzFeed executive, novel.

sentences.en: But I do think we’ve figured out a model that is quality journalism built around great journalists, paired with really large scale convening that is building both great journalism and a really good business, a profitable business — which is something that is, to me as a former BuzzFeed executive, novel.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为我们已经找到了一种模式，即围绕伟大的记者建立高质量的新闻业，并与真正大规模的会议相结合，既建立了伟大的新闻业，又建立了一个真正好的企业，一个有利可图的企业——对于我作为一名前 BuzzFeed 高管来说，这是一种新颖的东西。

blocks.html_en: A profitable digital media business is in short supply these days. It’s funny, I was looking over our conversation from three years ago. You had just published your book Traffic, which was basically about what I would call the millennial digital media moment and everyone chasing massive scale.

sentences.en: A profitable digital media business is in short supply these days.
sentences.zh: 如今，盈利的数字媒体业务供不应求。

sentences.en: It’s funny, I was looking over our conversation from three years ago.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我正在回顾我们三年前的谈话。

sentences.en: You had just published your book Traffic, which was basically about what I would call the millennial digital media moment and everyone chasing massive scale.
sentences.zh: 您刚刚出版了《流量》一书，这本书基本上是关于我所说的千禧年数字媒体时刻和每个人都在追求大规模的内容。

blocks.html_en: “The platforms are going to deliver tons of traffic to us and then we’ll collect pennies and we’ll all get rich.” This was a pretty common thesis. It feels like you’re saying you’ve turned away from that. You’ve learned the lesson of that time.

sentences.en: “The platforms are going to deliver tons of traffic to us and then we’ll collect pennies and we’ll all get rich.”
sentences.zh: “这些平台将为我们带来大量流量，然后我们就能赚到钱，然后我们都会变得富有。”

sentences.en: This was a pretty common thesis.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很常见的论点。

sentences.en: It feels like you’re saying you’ve turned away from that.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像你在说你已经放弃了这一点。

sentences.en: You’ve learned the lesson of that time.
sentences.zh: 你已经吸取了那次的教训。

blocks.html_en: Our chief revenue officer, Rachel Oppenheim, likes to joke that my next book will be called No Traffic, but we are really building an anti-scale business. The luxury of starting in that moment, in the rubble of the traffic apocalypse, was obviously not the path to success.

sentences.en: Our chief revenue officer, Rachel Oppenheim, likes to joke that my next book will be called No Traffic, but we are really building an anti-scale business.
sentences.zh: 我们的首席营收官雷切尔·奥本海姆 (Rachel Oppenheim) 喜欢开玩笑说我的下一本书将被称为《No Traffic》，但我们实际上正在建立一项反规模业务。

sentences.en: The luxury of starting in that moment, in the rubble of the traffic apocalypse, was obviously not the path to success.
sentences.zh: 在交通灾难的废墟中，在那一刻出发的奢侈，显然不是成功之路。

blocks.html_en: We had to think a lot about targeting and building a very specific audience. The thing that I have kind of come to realize in all these conversations… I listen to your show. We have a show about media that we yap about this on. What’s the future of media? Is it live? We were just talking about it. Who knows?

sentences.en: We had to think a lot about targeting and building a very specific audience.
sentences.zh: 我们必须认真思考如何定位和建立非常特定的受众群体。

sentences.en: The thing that I have kind of come to realize in all these conversations…
sentences.zh: 在所有这些谈话中我逐渐意识到的事情......

sentences.en: I listen to your show.
sentences.zh: 我听你的节目。

sentences.en: We have a show about media that we yap about this on.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个关于媒体的节目，我们在节目中对此大喊大叫。

sentences.en: What’s the future of media?
sentences.zh: 自媒体的未来是什么？

sentences.en: Is it live?
sentences.zh: 是直播吗？

sentences.en: We were just talking about it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在谈论它。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道？

blocks.html_en: But in journalism, I have a lot of conviction that great stories aren’t going anywhere. The need for high-quality insight isn’t going anywhere. Great reporters aren’t going anywhere. What surface this all lives on is up for grabs, and you can’t be too ideological about that.

sentences.en: But in journalism, I have a lot of conviction that great stories aren’t going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但在新闻业，我坚信伟大的故事不会消失。

sentences.en: The need for high-quality insight isn’t going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 对高质量洞察力的需求不会消失。

sentences.en: Great reporters aren’t going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 伟大的记者哪儿也不去。

sentences.en: What surface this all lives on is up for grabs, and you can’t be too ideological about that.
sentences.zh: 这一切赖以生存的表面是什么，都是有待争夺的，你不能对此抱有太多的意识形态。

blocks.html_en: You say surface, I always say distribution.

sentences.en: You say surface, I always say distribution.
sentences.zh: 你说表面，我总是说分布。

blocks.html_en: Yeah.

A theme on Decoder that we come back to over and over again is your distribution shapes what you make. It’s just inevitable. The medium is the message, to borrow that framing. If surfaces — if distribution — are up for grabs, what are you holding onto?

sentences.en: A theme on Decoder that we come back to over and over again is your distribution shapes what you make.
sentences.zh: 我们一遍又一遍地回顾 Decoder 的一个主题是，你的分布决定了你所做的事情。

sentences.en: It’s just inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: The medium is the message, to borrow that framing.
sentences.zh: 借用这个框架，媒介就是信息。

sentences.en: If surfaces — if distribution — are up for grabs, what are you holding onto?
sentences.zh: 如果表面（如果是分布）可供争夺，那么您会抓住什么？

blocks.html_en: I actually don’t buy that thesis, or at least I’m resisting that thesis because for the audience, the pull of distribution is incredibly powerful. The core thesis of BuzzFeed was we cracked the distribution and built for the distribution. Maybe I’m overreacting a little to that, but we definitely think all the time about how we want to reach political leaders and business leaders. We want to reach nonprofit leaders, and we want to reach people making decisions.

sentences.en: I actually don’t buy that thesis, or at least I’m resisting that thesis because for the audience, the pull of distribution is incredibly powerful.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我并不相信这个论点，或者至少我抵制这个论点，因为对于观众来说，发行的吸引力是非常强大的。

sentences.en: The core thesis of BuzzFeed was we cracked the distribution and built for the distribution.
sentences.zh: BuzzFeed 的核心论点是我们破解了发行版并为发行版而构建。

sentences.en: Maybe I’m overreacting a little to that, but we definitely think all the time about how we want to reach political leaders and business leaders.
sentences.zh: 也许我对此反应有点过度，但我们确实一直在思考我们希望如何接触政治领导人和商界领袖。

sentences.en: We want to reach nonprofit leaders, and we want to reach people making decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们希望接触非营利组织的领导者，我们希望接触做出决策的人们。

blocks.html_en: We want to reach them in person. We reach them a lot in email. We reach them on the web, we reach them in video, but we’re thinking about that same audience across media, and in fact, I think video is particularly interesting because of the pull. Videos are placed on the web in terms of the place you can get massive scale.

sentences.en: We want to reach them in person.
sentences.zh: 我们希望亲自与他们联系。

sentences.en: We reach them a lot in email.
sentences.zh: 我们经常通过电子邮件联系他们。

sentences.en: We reach them on the web, we reach them in video, but we’re thinking about that same audience across media, and in fact, I think video is particularly interesting because of the pull.
sentences.zh: 我们通过网络接触他们，通过视频接触他们，但我们正在考虑跨媒体的相同受众，事实上，我认为视频因为吸引力而特别有趣。

sentences.en: Videos are placed on the web in terms of the place you can get massive scale.
sentences.zh: 视频被放置在网络上，以便可以大规模使用。

blocks.html_en: Then conversely, where there’s a pull of massive scale to create the biggest pull is just to be hyper-polarizing and find ways to create polarizing confrontation. That’s how you go viral, or one of the best ways at least, and we’re trying hard to build the discipline to resist that pull of distribution.

sentences.en: Then conversely, where there’s a pull of massive scale to create the biggest pull is just to be hyper-polarizing and find ways to create polarizing confrontation.
sentences.zh: 相反，如果有大规模的拉力来创造最大的拉力，那就是超级极化，并找到制造极化对抗的方法。

sentences.en: That’s how you go viral, or one of the best ways at least, and we’re trying hard to build the discipline to resist that pull of distribution.
sentences.zh: 这就是病毒式传播的方式，或者至少是最好的方式之一，我们正在努力建立纪律来抵制这种分发的吸引力。

blocks.html_en: We’re already deep into the weeds. I hope that listeners can tell Ben and I like talking to each other about these things.

sentences.en: We’re already deep into the weeds.
sentences.zh: 我们已经深入杂草之中了。

sentences.en: I hope that listeners can tell Ben and I like talking to each other about these things.
sentences.zh: 我希望听众能够告诉本和我喜欢互相谈论这些事情。

sentences.en: But for news there really is, and you need to be careful.

sentences.en: If you’re reaching people in a very focused way in various particular environments — in person, in email, in video — that’s a case you can really credibly make to advertisers.

sentences.en: It’s not the only answer, but it is one.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Everyone loves the word “convening.”

blocks.html_en: We’re going to come to it because there’s a relationship between needing to get everyone in the room and then covering them, which I personally find fascinating.

sentences.en: We’re going to come to it because there’s a relationship between needing to get everyone in the room and then covering them, which I personally find fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以会谈到这个问题，是因为需要让每个人都到场然后覆盖他们之间存在着某种关系，我个人觉得这很有趣。

blocks.html_en: It’s booking. You had to not insult me for weeks to get me here.

sentences.en: It’s booking.
sentences.zh: 正在预订。

sentences.en: You had to not insult me for weeks to get me here.
sentences.zh: 你必须连续几个星期不侮辱我才能把我带到这里。

blocks.html_en: [Laughs] Or did I nag you every single day until you showed up?

sentences.en: [Laughs] Or did I nag you every single day until you showed up?
sentences.zh: [笑] 还是我每天都在唠叨你直到你出现？

blocks.html_en: Tell me about the revenue split between those things. Are you mostly making money on journalism? Are you mostly making money in events? Which is higher?

sentences.en: Tell me about the revenue split between those things.
sentences.zh: 告诉我这些东西之间的收入分配情况。

sentences.en: Are you mostly making money on journalism?
sentences.zh: 您主要靠新闻业赚钱吗？

sentences.en: Are you mostly making money in events?
sentences.zh: 您主要通过活动赚钱吗？

sentences.en: Which is higher?
sentences.zh: 哪个更高？

blocks.html_en: It’s just about 50/50.

sentences.en: It’s just about 50/50.

blocks.html_en: Is there a pull in either direction or are you trying to grow them both the same way?

sentences.en: Is there a pull in either direction or are you trying to grow them both the same way?
sentences.zh: 是否存在向任一方向的拉力，或者您是否试图以相同的方式使它们同时增长？

blocks.html_en: We’re a startup. We’re opportunistic. The convening business grew a lot faster. My partner, Justin Smith, has been building businesses like that. He was CEO of The Atlantic and Bloomberg. I’s much more his experience than mine.

sentences.en: We’re a startup.
sentences.zh: 我们是一家初创公司。

sentences.en: We’re opportunistic.
sentences.zh: 我们是机会主义者。

sentences.en: The convening business grew a lot faster.
sentences.zh: 召集业务增长速度更快。

sentences.en: My partner, Justin Smith, has been building businesses like that.
sentences.zh: 我的合作伙伴贾斯汀·史密斯（Justin Smith）一直在创建这样的企业。

sentences.en: He was CEO of The Atlantic and Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任《大西洋月刊》和《彭博社》的首席执行官。

sentences.en: I’s much more his experience than mine.
sentences.zh: 我对他的经历比对我的经历要多得多。

blocks.html_en: But he came in with this thesis, which I bought into, that basically convening was the business that you could stand up fastest and make profitable fastest, that was a journalism business. We launched hard into that space because it takes longer to build a digital advertising business: you’ve got to build that digital audience. We launched with that and then it’s just taken off in a way we, or at least I, didn’t see. I didn’t imagine that we’d be really competing with Davos this soon.

sentences.en: But he came in with this thesis, which I bought into, that basically convening was the business that you could stand up fastest and make profitable fastest, that was a journalism business.
sentences.zh: 但他带着这样的论点进来，我也认同这一点：基本上，召集是你能最快站稳脚跟、最快盈利的行业，这就是新闻业。

sentences.en: We launched hard into that space because it takes longer to build a digital advertising business: you’ve got to build that digital audience.
sentences.zh: 我们大力进入这个领域是因为建立数字广告业务需要更长的时间：你必须建立数字受众。

sentences.en: We launched with that and then it’s just taken off in a way we, or at least I, didn’t see.
sentences.zh: 我们以此为起点，然后它就以一种我们（或者至少是我）没有看到的方式起飞了。

sentences.en: I didn’t imagine that we’d be really competing with Davos this soon.
sentences.zh: 我没想到我们这么快就能真正与达沃斯竞争。

blocks.html_en: I want to come back to that, too. When you launched, I remember part of the plan was to go to subscriptions. You were going to build this elite audience. You’re going to charge them lots of money. It was there in the very beginning.

sentences.en: I want to come back to that, too.
sentences.zh: 我也想回到这一点。

sentences.en: When you launched, I remember part of the plan was to go to subscriptions.
sentences.zh: 当你推出时，我记得计划的一部分是订阅。

sentences.en: You were going to build this elite audience.
sentences.zh: 你要建立这个精英观众群。

sentences.en: You’re going to charge them lots of money.
sentences.zh: 你会向他们收取很多钱。

sentences.en: It was there in the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 它一开始就在那里。

blocks.html_en: Was that part of the plan?

sentences.en: Was that part of the plan?
sentences.zh: 这是计划的一部分吗？

sentences.en: It was early on, it was part of the plan.
sentences.zh: 这是很早的事情，这是计划的一部分。

blocks.html_en: Startups, yeah.

sentences.en: Startups, yeah.
sentences.zh: 初创公司，是的。

blocks.html_en: You also said, “We barely need a website. It’s all going to be newsletters.”

sentences.en: You also said, “We barely need a website.
sentences.zh: 你还说，“我们几乎不需要一个网站。

sentences.zh: 这一切都将成为时事通讯。”

blocks.html_en: Oh, we did talk about that. You were one of those website people.

sentences.en: Oh, we did talk about that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们确实讨论过这个。

sentences.en: You were one of those website people.
sentences.zh: 您是那些网站人员之一。

sentences.zh: 直到今天。

blocks.html_en: The last.

sentences.en: The last.
sentences.zh: 最后一个。

blocks.html_en: The last website on earth, that’s TheVerge.com. That all changed for reasons that things change with startups, but the media industry and distribution changed around it. Was there a moment where you said, “We can keep it free,” because you are one of the last free websites?

sentences.en: The last website on earth, that’s TheVerge.com.
sentences.zh: 地球上最后一个网站是 TheVerge.com。

sentences.en: That all changed for reasons that things change with startups, but the media industry and distribution changed around it.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生了变化，原因是初创公司的情况发生了变化，但媒体行业和发行围绕它发生了变化。

sentences.zh: 您是否曾说过，“我们可以保持免费”，因为您是最后的免费网站之一？

blocks.html_en: In my memory, we always thought at some point we’d do subscriptions, but in my experience you just cannot be ideological about revenue. It’s hard enough to build a business in news without getting all hung up on the values of the different revenue streams.

sentences.en: In my memory, we always thought at some point we’d do subscriptions, but in my experience you just cannot be ideological about revenue.
sentences.zh: 在我的记忆中，我们总是认为在某个时候我们会进行订阅，但根据我的经验，你不能对收入抱有意识形态。

sentences.en: It’s hard enough to build a business in news without getting all hung up on the values of the different revenue streams.
sentences.zh: 如果不完全关注不同收入来源的价值，就很难在新闻领域建立业务。

blocks.html_en: Advertising-based publishers will tell you that democracy can only survive in a world where there aren’t paywalls. Subscription publishers will tell you that advertising is corrupting. At some point you realize everyone’s just talking about their book and that sometimes they’re already in a tough business and they’re talking themselves out of incremental opportunities and really successful media companies.

sentences.en: Advertising-based publishers will tell you that democracy can only survive in a world where there aren’t paywalls.
sentences.zh: 以广告为基础的出版商会告诉你，民主只能在没有付费墙的世界中生存。

sentences.en: Subscription publishers will tell you that advertising is corrupting.
sentences.zh: 订阅出版商会告诉你广告正在腐败。

sentences.en: At some point you realize everyone’s just talking about their book and that sometimes they’re already in a tough business and they’re talking themselves out of incremental opportunities and really successful media companies.
sentences.zh: 在某些时候，你意识到每个人都只是在谈论他们的书，有时他们已经陷入困境，他们正在说服自己放弃增量机会和真正成功的媒体公司。

blocks.html_en: If you look at Disney or The New York Times, what business are they in? They’re actually in a bunch of different businesses. They’re managing them all really carefully. Our view is that if at some point it makes sense to do subscriptions, we’ll totally do them, but we don’t really see it as an ideological choice. When you’re starting a company, you just can’t do that many things at the same time.

sentences.en: If you look at Disney or The New York Times, what business are they in?
sentences.zh: 如果你看看迪士尼或纽约时报，他们从事什么业务？

sentences.en: They’re actually in a bunch of different businesses.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上从事许多不同的业务。

sentences.en: They’re managing them all really carefully.
sentences.zh: 他们非常仔细地管理它们。

sentences.en: Our view is that if at some point it makes sense to do subscriptions, we’ll totally do them, but we don’t really see it as an ideological choice.
sentences.zh: 我们的观点是，如果在某些时候进行订阅有意义，我们完全会这样做，但我们并不真正将其视为一种意识形态选择。

sentences.en: When you’re starting a company, you just can’t do that many things at the same time.

blocks.html_en: Also, I would say more broadly, and I got mocked for this at some point, but we are insanely ambitious about our long-term growth. We really are trying to build, over decades, a huge global company, and subscriptions are a trade-off that caps your growth in some ways. That’s something we think about too. But that said, we’re really trying to build a good business, and if subscriptions are a part of that, at some point we’ll certainly be a part of that.

sentences.en: Also, I would say more broadly, and I got mocked for this at some point, but we are insanely ambitious about our long-term growth.

sentences.en: We really are trying to build, over decades, a huge global company, and subscriptions are a trade-off that caps your growth in some ways.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，我们确实在努力建立一家大型全球性公司，而订阅是一种权衡，在某些方面限制了你的成长。

blocks.html_en: You launched with a lot of ambition. You’re the first news organization of your kind to say, “We’re going to cover Africa a lot, we’re going to cover the Gulf a lot in various ways.”

sentences.en: You launched with a lot of ambition.
sentences.zh: 您一开始就雄心勃勃。

blocks.html_en: That ambition was that those markets are under-covered, and you’re going to provide new information that readers aren’t necessarily getting from other places. You’ll build up that audience and then monetize them in some specific way. Has that thesis proved out?

sentences.en: That ambition was that those markets are under-covered, and you’re going to provide new information that readers aren’t necessarily getting from other places.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是那些市场未被充分报道，并且您将提供读者不一定从其他地方获得的新信息。

sentences.zh: 您将建立这些受众，然后以某种特定方式将其货币化。

sentences.en: Has that thesis proved out?
sentences.zh: 那篇论文被证明了吗？

blocks.html_en: Yes, and I would say when we launched, this was the thing that was most confusing to people. That Justin and I had worked in global news and had these real ambitions for it, but also were very careful about sequencing.

sentences.zh: 贾斯汀和我曾在全球新闻领域工作过，对此抱有真正的抱负，但在排序方面也非常谨慎。

blocks.html_en: When we launched, we were in the US, Brooklyn, Washington, on Wall Street, Silicon Valley, and Africa. sentences.zh: 我们在 BuzzFeed 就有过这样的经历。

sentences.en: This is part of why I was so excited to do some of it with Justin, because Justin had successfully built businesses in these other markets.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我如此兴奋与贾斯汀一起做一些事情的部分原因，因为贾斯汀已经在这些其他市场成功建立了业务。

sentences.en: At BuzzFeed we’d gone in, built big audiences, and we’d seen in Brazil, in the UK, in Japan this very intense engagement.
sentences.zh: 在 BuzzFeed，我们进入并建立了大量受众，我们在巴西、英国、日本都看到了这种非常激烈的参与。

sentences.en: People wanted independent journalism of this new digital and independent kind.
sentences.zh: 人们想要这种新的数字化和独立的独立新闻。

blocks.html_en: I remember in the first meeting we were talking about this, Eric Hippeau, this very smart, long-time digital investor was like, “Do not do this. You will never make any money and you’ll have to shut it all down.” We said, “Ah, forget it, old timer.” He was totally correct. We just never figured out how to reliably monetize them.

sentences.en: I remember in the first meeting we were talking about this, Eric Hippeau, this very smart, long-time digital investor was like, “Do not do this.
sentences.zh: 我记得在第一次会议上我们讨论过这个问题，埃里克·希波（Eric Hippeau），这位非常聪明的长期数字投资者说，“不要这样做。

sentences.en: You will never make any money and you’ll have to shut it all down.”
sentences.zh: 你永远赚不到钱，你必须把它全部关闭。”

sentences.en: We said, “Ah, forget it, old timer.”
sentences.zh: 我们说：“啊，算了，老家伙。”

sentences.en: He was totally correct.
sentences.zh: 他是完全正确的。

sentences.en: We just never figured out how to reliably monetize them.
sentences.zh: 我们只是从未弄清楚如何可靠地将它们货币化。

blocks.html_en: Even when you could, you’d say, “The Brazilian edition was profitable this year, but bad news, they have currency controls, so the money stays in Brazil.” “Oh, nobody told us that.”

sentences.en: Even when you could, you’d say, “The Brazilian edition was profitable this year, but bad news, they have currency controls, so the money stays in Brazil.”
sentences.zh: 即使可以，你也会说，“巴西版今年盈利了，但坏消息是，他们有货币管制，所以钱留在巴西。”

sentences.en: “Oh, nobody told us that.”
sentences.zh: “哦，没人告诉我们这个。”

blocks.html_en: How have you solved for it now?

sentences.en: How have you solved for it now?
sentences.zh: 你现在是怎么解决的？

blocks.html_en: We’re pretty careful about keeping the costs low and growing the verticals with local revenue. There’s also a lot of value in these huge gatherings that we’re building, that they are fundamentally global, whether it’s in Silicon Valley or in Washington. Building these global networks of CEOs and political leaders feeds that network. That’s been valuable. But I don’t know, we’re careful as part of it. That’s one thing I learned from BuzzFeed.

sentences.en: We’re pretty careful about keeping the costs low and growing the verticals with local revenue.
sentences.zh: 我们非常谨慎地保持低成本并利用当地收入来发展垂直行业。

sentences.en: There’s also a lot of value in these huge gatherings that we’re building, that they are fundamentally global, whether it’s in Silicon Valley or in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们正在建立的这些大型聚会也有很多价值，它们基本上是全球性的，无论是在硅谷还是在华盛顿。

sentences.en: Building these global networks of CEOs and political leaders feeds that network.
sentences.zh: 建立这些首席执行官和政治领导人的全球网络可以为该网络提供支持。

sentences.en: That’s been valuable.
sentences.zh: 这很有价值。

sentences.en: But I don’t know, we’re careful as part of it.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道，我们对此很小心。

sentences.en: That’s one thing I learned from BuzzFeed.
sentences.zh: 这是我从 BuzzFeed 学到的一件事。

blocks.html_en: The high-flying VC era has produced a generation of very conservative media operators.

sentences.en: The high-flying VC era has produced a generation of very conservative media operators.
sentences.zh: 风头正劲的风险投资时代造就了一代非常保守的媒体运营商。

blocks.html_en: That’s right.

sentences.en: That’s right.
sentences.zh: 这是正确的。

blocks.html_en: I think that’s fascinating. The other big innovation I want to talk to you about from the beginning of Semafor, and then I want to start talking about what you’re doing now, the Semaform.

sentences.en: I think that’s fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有趣。

sentences.en: The other big innovation I want to talk to you about from the beginning of Semafor, and then I want to start talking about what you’re doing now, the Semaform.
sentences.zh: 我想和你们谈论 Semafor 之初的另一项重大创新，然后我想开始谈论你们现在正在做的事情，Semaform。

blocks.html_en: You launched with this way of writing an article. You still use it to this day. I see it all the time. The thesis was that it would just sort of make it simpler to understand what all the different pieces are. I always thought that was funny because you were chasing the most elite audience possible, and presumably they could already understand what was going on.

sentences.en: You launched with this way of writing an article.
sentences.zh: 您以这种写文章的方式开始了。

sentences.en: You still use it to this day.
sentences.zh: 直到今天你还在使用它。

sentences.en: I see it all the time.
sentences.zh: 我经常看到它。

sentences.en: The thesis was that it would just sort of make it simpler to understand what all the different pieces are.
sentences.zh: 其论点是，它只是让人们更容易理解所有不同的部分是什么。

sentences.en: I always thought that was funny because you were chasing the most elite audience possible, and presumably they could already understand what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为这很有趣，因为你正在追逐尽可能最精英的观众，并且想必他们已经能够理解正在发生的事情。

blocks.html_en: That’s the problem. They could understand what was going on. And what is going on in a newspaper article is we have a who, what, where, why sentence.

sentences.en: That’s the problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: They could understand what was going on.
sentences.zh: 他们能够理解发生了什么事。

sentences.en: And what is going on in a newspaper article is we have a who, what, where, why sentence.
sentences.zh: 在报纸文章中，我们有一个“谁”、“什么”、“哪里”、“为什么”句子。

blocks.html_en: And then you have another sentence that says the same thing. And then you have a paragraph, and then you have a quote that is from an expert, but it just reflects whatever the reporter thinks and they’ve picked the expert with their bias to repeat. And then you have an unsupported paragraph of random theories called the nut graf.

sentences.en: And then you have another sentence that says the same thing.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有另一个句子说同样的事情。

sentences.en: And then you have a paragraph, and then you have a quote that is from an expert, but it just reflects whatever the reporter thinks and they’ve picked the expert with their bias to repeat.
sentences.zh: 然后你有一个段落，然后你有一个来自专家的引言，但这只是反映了记者的想法，他们选择了带有偏见的专家来重复。

sentences.en: And then you have an unsupported paragraph of random theories called the nut graf.
sentences.zh: 然后你就有了一段不受支持的随机理论，称为坚果图。

blocks.html_en: Everything else is just chronological order. Particularly the “an expert in disinformation says this” or “an expert in democracy says this,” any reader sees, “This is what the publication thinks, this what the journalist thinks. Why don’t they just say it rather than do this weird move of filtering your biases through an expert?” And particularly with a sophisticated audience, they’re in on the joke a bit. There are two sides to it because one is that the journalist is required to smuggle their opinion or their analysis in other people’s voices. The other is that really good beat reporters are real experts.

sentences.en: Everything else is just chronological order.
sentences.zh: 其他一切都只是按时间顺序排列。

sentences.en: Particularly the “an expert in disinformation says this” or “an expert in democracy says this,” any reader sees, “This is what the publication thinks, this what the journalist thinks.
sentences.zh: 特别是“虚假信息专家这样说”或“民主专家这样说”，任何读者都会看到，“这就是出版物的想法，这就是记者的想法。

sentences.en: Why don’t they just say it rather than do this weird move of filtering your biases through an expert?”
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不直接说出来，而是采取这种奇怪的举动，通过专家过滤你的偏见？”

sentences.en: And particularly with a sophisticated audience, they’re in on the joke a bit.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于经验丰富的观众来说，他们有点开玩笑。

sentences.en: There are two sides to it because one is that the journalist is required to smuggle their opinion or their analysis in other people’s voices.
sentences.zh: 它有两个方面，因为一方面是记者被要求以其他人的声音来传达他们的观点或分析。

sentences.en: The other is that really good beat reporters are real experts.
sentences.zh: 另一个是真正优秀的记者都是真正的专家。

blocks.html_en: A sophisticated reader actually wants to know what Maggie Haberman thinks to a really high degree. Because the other deal in the newspaper is that you conceal your own analysis and opinion. On both sides of that, the reader is sort of losing out. You’re treating them like an idiot because you’re smuggling bias and opinion in, and then also — and this is particularly true of really senior experienced beat reporters — people read Reed Albergotti or Burgess Everett and want to know what they think. So tell me what you actually think.

sentences.en: A sophisticated reader actually wants to know what Maggie Haberman thinks to a really high degree.
sentences.zh: 一个老练的读者实际上想知道玛吉·哈伯曼在很大程度上的想法。

sentences.en: Because the other deal in the newspaper is that you conceal your own analysis and opinion.
sentences.zh: 因为报纸上的另一项交易是你隐瞒自己的分析和观点。

sentences.en: On both sides of that, the reader is sort of losing out.
sentences.zh: 在这两个方面，读者都有点失败。

sentences.en: You’re treating them like an idiot because you’re smuggling bias and opinion in, and then also — and this is particularly true of really senior experienced beat reporters — people read Reed Albergotti or Burgess Everett and want to know what they think.
sentences.zh: 你把他们当作白痴一样对待，因为你偷偷带入了偏见和观点，而且——对于真正资深的经验丰富的记者来说尤其如此——人们读了里德·阿尔伯戈蒂或伯吉斯·埃弗雷特，并想知道他们的想法。

sentences.en: So tell me what you actually think.
sentences.zh: 那么请告诉我你的真实想法。

blocks.html_en: The Semaform is an attempt to separate “here are the facts of the story we can all agree on” and “here’s the journalist’s analysis.” For an analysis to be interesting, there’s got to be some chance it can be wrong. Otherwise, it’s totally banal. We go out of our way to try to find somebody who disagrees with us to include that, too. People like that. It’s a bit of humility also.

sentences.en: The Semaform is an attempt to separate “here are the facts of the story we can all agree on” and “here’s the journalist’s analysis.”
sentences.zh: Semaform 试图区分“这是我们都同意的故事事实”和“这是记者的分析”。

sentences.en: For an analysis to be interesting, there’s got to be some chance it can be wrong.
sentences.zh: 为了使分析变得有趣，它必须有可能是错误的。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it’s totally banal.
sentences.zh: 否则，这完全是平庸的。

sentences.en: We go out of our way to try to find somebody who disagrees with us to include that, too.
sentences.zh: 我们不遗余力地试图找到不同意我们观点的人也将这一点包括在内。

sentences.en: People like that.
sentences.zh: 人们就是这样。

sentences.en: It’s a bit of humility also.
sentences.zh: 这也算是一种谦虚吧。

blocks.html_en: Back in my day, we just called this blogging.

sentences.en: Back in my day, we just called this blogging.
sentences.zh: 在我那个时代，我们称之为博客。

blocks.html_en: [Laughs] Blogging, yes.

sentences.en: [Laughs] Blogging, yes.
sentences.zh: [笑]写博客，是的。

blocks.html_en: I would just write down what I thought all the time.

sentences.en: I would just write down what I thought all the time.
sentences.zh: 我只会写下我一直以来的想法。

blocks.html_en: I would say this was influenced by blogging. I know, we’re all old bloggers now. It’s so embarrassing to explain to people that you used to have a blog.

sentences.en: I would say this was influenced by blogging.
sentences.zh: 我想说这是受到博客的影响。

sentences.en: I know, we’re all old bloggers now.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我们现在都是老博主了。

sentences.en: It’s so embarrassing to explain to people that you used to have a blog.
sentences.zh: 向人们解释你曾经有一个博客真是太尴尬了。

blocks.html_en: What do I run to this day? It’s still fundamentally the reporters saying what they think.

sentences.en: What do I run to this day?
sentences.zh: 我跑到今天做什么？

sentences.en: It’s still fundamentally the reporters saying what they think.
sentences.zh: 本质上仍然是记者说出他们的想法。

blocks.html_en: Someday you’ll be explaining to people you had a podcast.

sentences.en: Someday you’ll be explaining to people you had a podcast.
sentences.zh: 有一天你会向人们解释你有一个播客。

blocks.html_en: It’ll just be my VR avatar talking to your VR avatar.

sentences.en: It’ll just be my VR avatar talking to your VR avatar.
sentences.zh: 这只是我的 VR 化身与你的 VR 化身对话。

blocks.html_en: [Laughs] It will be another silly word, yeah.

sentences.en: [Laughs] It will be another silly word, yeah.
sentences.zh: [笑]这又是一个愚蠢的词，是的。

blocks.html_en: No legs. It’ll be great. The reason I ask about the format in particular is that my thesis is that distribution and formats shape each other. Semaform was a new format. It was a way to reach an audience and say, “We know you’re not stupid. We’re going to show you the structure of the story out loud.” Has it been successful? Has it actually succeeded in attracting an audience or is it just the trademark of how you do things now?

sentences.en: No legs.
sentences.zh: 没有腿。

sentences.en: It’ll be great.
sentences.zh: 会很棒的。

sentences.en: The reason I ask about the format in particular is that my thesis is that distribution and formats shape each other.
sentences.zh: 我特别询问格式的原因是我的论点是分发和格式相互影响。

sentences.en: Semaform was a new format.
sentences.zh: Semaform 是一种新格式。

sentences.en: It was a way to reach an audience and say, “We know you’re not stupid.
sentences.zh: 这是一种接触观众并说：“我们知道你并不傻。

sentences.en: We’re going to show you the structure of the story out loud.”
sentences.zh: 我们将大声向你展示故事的结构。”

sentences.en: Has it been successful?
sentences.zh: 成功了吗？

sentences.en: Has it actually succeeded in attracting an audience or is it just the trademark of how you do things now?
sentences.zh: 它真的成功地吸引了观众吗？还是这只是你现在做事方式的标志？

blocks.html_en: We hear a lot about it from our audience. People really like it. We also do a lot of shorter form stuff, and so that’s not always broken out that way. But that value of, “We’re going to be really humble, we’re going to be assertive about what we think, but also very, very open to disagreement, very clear about the difference between a fact and analysis,” is core to our DNA and everything we do, including in the events.

sentences.en: We hear a lot about it from our audience.
sentences.zh: 我们从观众那里听到了很多关于它的事情。

sentences.en: People really like it.
sentences.zh: 人们真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: We also do a lot of shorter form stuff, and so that’s not always broken out that way.
sentences.zh: 我们还做了很多简短的内容，所以并不总是这样。

sentences.en: But that value of, “We’re going to be really humble, we’re going to be assertive about what we think, but also very, very open to disagreement, very clear about the difference between a fact and analysis,” is core to our DNA and everything we do, including in the events.
sentences.zh: 但“我们将非常谦虚，我们将对我们的想法保持自信，但也对分歧非常非常开放，非常清楚事实与分析之间的差异”，这是我们的 DNA 和我们所做的一切（包括在活动中）的核心。

blocks.html_en: Let me ask you Decoder questions. I want to just talk about what’s going on in this industry now. Because you’ve learned a lot and it’s been almost four years that Semafor has been going. Those are all the big early bets and I just want to check in on them. How big is Semafor now?

sentences.en: Let me ask you Decoder questions.
sentences.zh: 让我问你解码器问题。

sentences.en: I want to just talk about what’s going on in this industry now.
sentences.zh: 我只想谈谈现在这个行业正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Because you’ve learned a lot and it’s been almost four years that Semafor has been going.
sentences.zh: 因为你学到了很多东西，而且 Semafor 已经运行了近四年了。

sentences.en: Those are all the big early bets and I just want to check in on them.
sentences.zh: 这些都是早期的大赌注，我只是想检查一下。

sentences.en: How big is Semafor now?
sentences.zh: Semafor现在有多大？

blocks.html_en: We’ve got about 60 journalists, and more than 100 employees.

sentences.en: We’ve got about 60 journalists, and more than 100 employees.
sentences.zh: 我们有大约 60 名记者和 100 多名员工。

blocks.html_en: How is all that structured?

sentences.en: How is all that structured?
sentences.zh: 这一切是如何构建的？

blocks.html_en: I’d say more than 100. It’s probably about half journalists, half a commercial team that includes revenue and a great events production team. We do all that stuff in-house. Part of the luxury of a startup and part of the challenge in news is that — and I think you’re inside at the moment one or two companies that have cracked this — there’s not a lot of talent on the business side of news for obvious reasons. It’s a terrible business.

sentences.en: I’d say more than 100.
sentences.zh: 我想说超过100个。

sentences.en: It’s probably about half journalists, half a commercial team that includes revenue and a great events production team.
sentences.zh: 大概一半是记者，一半是商业团队（包括收入）和一个大型活动制作团队。

sentences.en: We do all that stuff in-house.
sentences.zh: 我们在内部完成所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Part of the luxury of a startup and part of the challenge in news is that — and I think you’re inside at the moment one or two companies that have cracked this — there’s not a lot of talent on the business side of news for obvious reasons.
sentences.zh: 初创公司的奢侈之处和新闻挑战的一部分是——我想你现在有一两家已经解决了这个问题的公司——出于显而易见的原因，新闻业务方面的人才并不多。

sentences.en: It’s a terrible business.
sentences.zh: 这是一项糟糕的生意。

blocks.html_en: You go to Harvard Business School and 30 percent of those people go into enterprise sales and .01 percent go into media, for the obvious reason that they like to make money. They look around for where the money is and it’s not in media.

sentences.en: You go to Harvard Business School and 30 percent of those people go into enterprise sales and .01 percent go into media, for the obvious reason that they like to make money.
sentences.zh: 你去哈佛商学院，其中 30% 的人从事企业销售工作，0.01% 的人从事媒体工作，原因很明显，他们喜欢赚钱。

sentences.en: They look around for where the money is and it’s not in media.
sentences.zh: 他们四处寻找钱的来源，但发现钱不在媒体中。

blocks.html_en: We’ve been incredibly aggressive about trying to recruit really, really great commercial operators and people on our revenue side. It’s fun to be in a place where the wattage on the business side is really, really high. That’s been a real luxury for us. We have bookers, we have producers, we have people thinking about the vibes and the music. We take all that stuff really seriously.

sentences.en: We’ve been incredibly aggressive about trying to recruit really, really great commercial operators and people on our revenue side.
sentences.zh: 我们非常积极地尝试招募真正非常优秀的商业运营商和收入方面的人员。

sentences.en: It’s fun to be in a place where the wattage on the business side is really, really high.
sentences.zh: 身处一个业务层面非常非常高的地方是很有趣的。

sentences.en: That’s been a real luxury for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说真是一种奢侈。

sentences.en: We have bookers, we have producers, we have people thinking about the vibes and the music.
sentences.zh: 我们有预订者，我们有制作人，我们有人思考氛围和音乐。

sentences.en: We take all that stuff really seriously.
sentences.zh: 我们非常认真地对待所有这些事情。

blocks.html_en: Do you have an in-house DJ?

sentences.en: Do you have an in-house DJ?
sentences.zh: 你们有内部 DJ 吗？

blocks.html_en: Would I call Brigitte Anders-Kraus an in-house DJ? I think that would be a reasonable thing to say.

sentences.en: Would I call Brigitte Anders-Kraus an in-house DJ?
sentences.zh: 我可以称 Brigitte Anders-Kraus 为内部 DJ 吗？

sentences.en: I think that would be a reasonable thing to say.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个合理的说法。

blocks.html_en: That’s pretty good.

sentences.en: That’s pretty good.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

blocks.html_en: I think she would object. She does a lot of other stuff too. She’s very efficient.

sentences.en: I think she would object.
sentences.zh: 我想她会反对。

sentences.en: She does a lot of other stuff too.
sentences.zh: 她还做了很多其他事情。

sentences.en: She’s very efficient.
sentences.zh: 她非常有效率。

blocks.html_en: When we did the code conference, I spent a lot of time thinking about the Spotify playlist.

sentences.en: When we did the code conference, I spent a lot of time thinking about the Spotify playlist.
sentences.zh: 当我们召开代码会议时，我花了很多时间思考 Spotify 播放列表。

blocks.html_en: You got to think about that stuff.

sentences.en: You got to think about that stuff.
sentences.zh: 你必须考虑一下那些事情。

blocks.html_en: Actually, that brings me to the other Decoder question I ask everybody. You have a lot of decisions to make. You’ve grown up a lot over the past four years at Semafor. How do you make decisions? What’s your framework?

sentences.en: Actually, that brings me to the other Decoder question I ask everybody.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这让我想到了我问大家的另一个解码器问题。

sentences.en: You have a lot of decisions to make.
sentences.zh: 你有很多决定要做。

sentences.en: You’ve grown up a lot over the past four years at Semafor.
sentences.zh: 过去四年来，您在 Semafor 成长了很多。

sentences.en: How do you make decisions?
sentences.zh: 你如何做决定？

sentences.en: What’s your framework?
sentences.zh: 你的框架是什么？

blocks.html_en: I personally make decisions very, very, very fast at very high volume. But I am very attentive to the people around me when they think it’s a mistake, and I’m quick to reverse them

sentences.en: I personally make decisions very, very, very fast at very high volume.
sentences.zh: 我个人在非常非常快的数量下做出决定。

sentences.en: But I am very attentive to the people around me when they think it’s a mistake, and I’m quick to reverse them
sentences.zh: 但当我周围的人认为这是一个错误时，我会非常关注他们，并且我会很快纠正他们

blocks.html_en: I care a lot about hiring great journalists and having people who I really trust and I rarely jam a decision down anybody’s throat. I want to be surrounded by people who are deep experts in what they’re doing, whether it’s managing or building AI tools or reporting. But I’m very happy to lose fights.

sentences.en: But I’m very happy to lose fights.

blocks.html_en: This is a new kind of business you’re describing. You want to make a lot of decisions fast. You’re growing in a lot of different areas. sentences.en: This is a new kind of business you’re describing.

sentences.en: You want to make a lot of decisions fast.
sentences.zh: 您想快速做出很多决定。

sentences.en: You’re growing in a lot of different areas.
sentences.zh: 你在很多不同的领域都在成长。

sentences.en: Every time I see you in person, I bring you a new journalism ethics problem.
sentences.zh: 每次我亲自见到你，我都会给你带来一个新的新闻道德问题。

sentences.en: This is a real recurring theme in our relationship.
sentences.zh: 这是我们关系中真正反复出现的主题。

sentences.en: I’m always struggling to be pure of heart.
sentences.zh: 我一直在努力保持内心的纯洁。

blocks.html_en: You come from the most corrupt corner of journalism, which is gadget reviews. You’ve appropriately figured out that in that dark cave, ethics is this incredible way for The Verge to distinguish itself.

sentences.zh: 你来自新闻业最腐败的角落，即电子产品评论。

sentences.en: You’ve appropriately figured out that in that dark cave, ethics is this incredible way for The Verge to distinguish itself.
sentences.zh: 你已经正确地认识到，在那个黑暗的洞穴里，道德是 The Verge 脱颖而出的不可思议的方式。

blocks.html_en: It’s literally what we say to our audience: “We are selling you this policy that we can’t be bought.” Maybe that’s the right thing. I look at some of the creators and I look at some of their Lamborghinis and I think maybe that’s the wrong thing. But that’s the way it goes.

sentences.en: It’s literally what we say to our audience: “We are selling you this policy that we can’t be bought.”
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对观众说的：“我们正在向你们出售我们无法购买的保单。”

sentences.en: Maybe that’s the right thing.
sentences.zh: 也许这是正确的事情。

sentences.en: I look at some of the creators and I look at some of their Lamborghinis and I think maybe that’s the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 我看了一些创作者，也看了他们的一些兰博基尼，我认为这也许是错误的。

sentences.en: But that’s the way it goes.
sentences.zh: 但事情就是这样。

sentences.en: I started by playing you that clip of Jonah Peretti saying if Facebook had only paid for news, the tech CEOs would’ve retained relevance and charisma.
sentences.zh: 我首先给你们播放了乔纳·佩雷蒂 (Jonah Peretti) 的一段视频，他说如果 Facebook 只为新闻付费，科技公司的首席执行官们就会保留相关性和魅力。

sentences.zh: 大卫·埃里森 (David Ellison) 收购了哥伦比亚广播公司新闻 (CBS News)，无论成功或失败。

sentences.en: He’s, depending on your point of view, either trying to get out of his Warner Bros.

blocks.html_en: Brendan Carr is fulminating at the FCC about what happens on the broadcast stations. He wrote an entire chapter of Project 2025 about regulating content moderation on platforms. I see more influence on the media from that side of the house than ever before.
