sentences.en: He wrote an entire chapter of Project 2025 about regulating content moderation on platforms.
sentences.zh: 他在 Project 2025 中撰写了有关规范平台内容审核的完整章节。

sentences.en: I see more influence on the media from that side of the house than ever before.
sentences.zh: 我看到房子那边对媒体的影响比以往任何时候都大。

blocks.html_en: That’s the audience that you aggressively try to go out and attract and monetize in different ways. How do you view all of that right now?

sentences.en: That’s the audience that you aggressively try to go out and attract and monetize in different ways.
sentences.zh: 这就是你积极尝试以不同方式走出去、吸引和货币化的受众。

sentences.en: How do you view all of that right now?
sentences.zh: 您现在如何看待这一切？

blocks.html_en: These are really different things. We’re in this moment of politicized wealthy individuals buying media companies and using them to curry favor with the White House. That’s just a very specific thing that is incredible.

sentences.en: These are really different things.
sentences.zh: 这些确实是不同的事情。

sentences.en: We’re in this moment of politicized wealthy individuals buying media companies and using them to curry favor with the White House.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于政治化的富人购买媒体公司并利用它们来讨好白宫的时刻。

sentences.en: That’s just a very specific thing that is incredible.
sentences.zh: 这只是一件非常具体的事情，令人难以置信。

blocks.html_en: In some sense, my view of the media has always been that if you actually are delivering something your audience wants, that gives you independence. They want you to be asking tough questions. They want you to be delivering them true facts and insight. That’s the path. There’s a temptation, particularly for places that don’t have strong business models, to start making ethical compromises and you see it all over the place.

sentences.en: In some sense, my view of the media has always been that if you actually are delivering something your audience wants, that gives you independence.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，我对媒体的看法一直是，如果你确实提供了观众想要的东西，那就给了你独立性。

sentences.en: They want you to be asking tough questions.
sentences.zh: 他们希望你提出尖锐的问题。

sentences.en: They want you to be delivering them true facts and insight.
sentences.zh: 他们希望您向他们提供真实的事实和见解。

sentences.en: That’s the path.
sentences.zh: 这就是路径。

sentences.en: There’s a temptation, particularly for places that don’t have strong business models, to start making ethical compromises and you see it all over the place.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易在道德上做出妥协，尤其是对于那些没有强大商业模式的地方，这种情况随处可见。

blocks.html_en: In a way, because you’re in the gadget review space, you see it so clearly. I think it’s true in every space. The core thing of journalism and what makes it interesting is the adversarial quality and the independence and the independence of the people you’re asking questions of, the people you’re covering. Businesses like advertising complicate that, but if you don’t hold onto that independence, you’re giving away the whole story.

sentences.en: In a way, because you’re in the gadget review space, you see it so clearly.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，因为您处于小工具评论空间，所以您可以清楚地看到它。

sentences.en: I think it’s true in every space.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在每个空间都是如此。

sentences.en: The core thing of journalism and what makes it interesting is the adversarial quality and the independence and the independence of the people you’re asking questions of, the people you’re covering.
sentences.zh: 新闻业的核心以及它的有趣之处在于它的对抗性以及你所提问的人、你所报道的人的独立性和独立性。

sentences.en: Businesses like advertising complicate that, but if you don’t hold onto that independence, you’re giving away the whole story.
sentences.zh: 像广告这样的企业会让事情变得复杂，但如果你不保持这种独立性，你就会泄露整个故事。

blocks.html_en: We think obsessively about that. For businesses that like innovating, it’s so important that you actually do not want to innovate in the field of ethics. That’s the one space where nobody should be innovating or you should be very, very careful, because if you think about why marketing conferences are so boring, it’s because they aren’t doing tough independent interviews with the people. Our events are interesting because we’re doing tough independent interviews and giving that away would be an enormous mistake.

sentences.en: We think obsessively about that.
sentences.zh: 我们着迷地思考这个问题。

sentences.en: For businesses that like innovating, it’s so important that you actually do not want to innovate in the field of ethics.
sentences.zh: 对于喜欢创新的企业来说，道德领域非常重要，以至于你实际上不想创新。

sentences.en: That’s the one space where nobody should be innovating or you should be very, very careful, because if you think about why marketing conferences are so boring, it’s because they aren’t doing tough independent interviews with the people.
sentences.zh: 这是一个没有人应该创新的领域，或者你应该非常非常小心，因为如果你思考为什么营销会议如此无聊，那是因为他们没有对人们进行艰难的独立采访。

sentences.en: Our events are interesting because we’re doing tough independent interviews and giving that away would be an enormous mistake.
sentences.zh: 我们的活动很有趣，因为我们正在进行艰难的独立采访，而泄露这些将是一个巨大的错误。

blocks.html_en: Can I ask you a really direct question about that?

sentences.en: Can I ask you a really direct question about that?
sentences.zh: 我可以问你一个非常直接的问题吗？

blocks.html_en: You’re doing Silicon Valley & The World, which is the big new conference. This is you saying you’re going to compete with Davos. You’re going to put on a bunch of conferences like this that compete on the biggest stage. You’re convening people, as I’ve been told.

sentences.en: You’re doing Silicon Valley & The World, which is the big new conference.
sentences.zh: 你们正在举办《硅谷与世界》，这是一场大型的新会议。

sentences.en: This is you saying you’re going to compete with Davos.
sentences.zh: 这是你说你要与达沃斯竞争。

sentences.en: You’re going to put on a bunch of conferences like this that compete on the biggest stage.
sentences.zh: 你将举办一系列这样的会议，在最大的舞台上竞争。

sentences.en: You’re convening people, as I’ve been told.
sentences.zh: 正如我听说的，你正在召集人们。

blocks.html_en: I looked at your announcement, and you were kind enough to invite me to it. On the board are Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella, and they’re advisors, but you’re going to do challenging journalism. How does that work?

sentences.en: I looked at your announcement, and you were kind enough to invite me to it.
sentences.zh: 我看了你的公告，你很友善地邀请我参加。

sentences.en: On the board are Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella, and they’re advisors, but you’re going to do challenging journalism.
sentences.zh: 董事会成员包括黄仁勋和萨蒂亚·纳德拉，他们是顾问，但你要做的是具有挑战性的新闻工作。

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 这是如何运作的？

blocks.html_en: It’s a reasonable question and it’s a feature of the convening business that is somewhat new business to me, too. But first of all, we’re thrilled that Jensen and Andy Jassy are going to be there and we’re going to be doing newsy on-stage interviews with them. It is a feature of that business.

sentences.en: It’s a reasonable question and it’s a feature of the convening business that is somewhat new business to me, too.
sentences.zh: 这是一个合理的问题，也是召集业务的一个特点，对我来说也是一个新业务。

sentences.en: But first of all, we’re thrilled that Jensen and Andy Jassy are going to be there and we’re going to be doing newsy on-stage interviews with them.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我们很高兴詹森和安迪·贾西将出席，我们将对他们进行新闻台上采访。

sentences.en: It is a feature of that business.
sentences.zh: 这是该业务的一个特点。

blocks.html_en: If you look at the way The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal and our other competitors like Bloomberg do it, part of building a community around these events and getting excitement around them is pulling the newsmakers you’ll be interviewing into the event in some way. The New York Times calls them task forces. The Wall Street Journal calls them a council. Bloomberg actually also calls them an advisory board. But the journalism is totally independent of them.

sentences.en: If you look at the way The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal and our other competitors like Bloomberg do it, part of building a community around these events and getting excitement around them is pulling the newsmakers you’ll be interviewing into the event in some way.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看《纽约时报》和《华尔街日报》以及我们的其他竞争对手（例如彭博社）的做法，就会发现围绕这些活动建立社区并激发人们的兴奋感的一部分就是以某种方式将你将采访的新闻人物拉入活动。

sentences.en: The New York Times calls them task forces.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》称他们为特别工作组。

sentences.en: The Wall Street Journal calls them a council.
sentences.zh: 《华尔街日报》称他们为理事会。

sentences.en: Bloomberg actually also calls them an advisory board.
sentences.zh: 彭博社实际上也称他们为顾问委员会。

sentences.en: But the journalism is totally independent of them.
sentences.zh: 但新闻业完全独立于他们。

blocks.html_en: But how does that work? I did Code Conference and I remember thinking, “I really need to get so-and-so CEO to show up on stage.” If the day before they get on the jet to show up in California, we say, “So-and-so’s CEO is deeply corrupt. Here’s our eight-month investigation…”

sentences.en: But how does that work?
sentences.zh: 但这是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: I did Code Conference and I remember thinking, “I really need to get so-and-so CEO to show up on stage.”
sentences.zh: 我参加了代码会议，我记得我当时想，“我真的需要让某某首席执行官出现在舞台上。”

sentences.en: If the day before they get on the jet to show up in California, we say, “So-and-so’s CEO is deeply corrupt.
sentences.zh: 如果在他们登上飞机前往加利福尼亚州的前一天，我们会说：“某某的首席执行官非常腐败。

sentences.en: Here’s our eight-month investigation…”
sentences.zh: 这是我们为期八个月的调查……”

blocks.html_en: They’re probably going to cancel on you.

sentences.en: They’re probably going to cancel on you.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会取消您的预订。

blocks.html_en: They’re probably going to cancel. And I thought, “That’s going to be fine. That’d be great actually.”

sentences.en: They’re probably going to cancel.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会取消。

sentences.en: And I thought, “That’s going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 我想：“那就没问题了。

sentences.en: That’d be great actually.”
sentences.zh: 实际上那就太好了。”

blocks.html_en: Yeah, totally.

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全可以。

blocks.html_en: Because I’ll get on stage and say, “They canceled because they can’t take it.” But at the same time, I knew that the people buying the tickets probably were buying the tickets to see so-and-so appear on stage. This never actually came to a head. This was never actually a problem. It was just always in my mind.

sentences.en: Because I’ll get on stage and say, “They canceled because they can’t take it.”
sentences.zh: 因为我会上台说：“他们取消了，因为他们无法接受。”

sentences.en: But at the same time, I knew that the people buying the tickets probably were buying the tickets to see so-and-so appear on stage.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我知道买票的人可能是为了看某某上台而买票。

sentences.en: This never actually came to a head.
sentences.zh: 这实际上从未达到紧要关头。

sentences.en: This was never actually a problem.
sentences.zh: 这实际上从来都不是问题。

sentences.en: It was just always in my mind.
sentences.zh: 它一直在我的脑海里。

blocks.html_en: Maybe you weren’t doing enough exposés.

sentences.en: Maybe you weren’t doing enough exposés.
sentences.zh: 也许你没有做足够的曝光。

blocks.html_en: I thought, “Should I be causing this problem more?” How do you think about that? You cover these companies at a really high level.

sentences.en: I thought, “Should I be causing this problem more?”
sentences.zh: 我想，“我应该更多地制造这个问题吗？”

sentences.en: How do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 您对此有何看法？

sentences.en: You cover these companies at a really high level.
sentences.zh: 您对这些公司的报道水平非常高。

blocks.html_en: We do obviously write stories that they don’t like all the time. We try really, really hard to be fair. We try not to sandbag people, but there are two different things. One is, “Did you write a story that upset them and they canceled on you?” You just have to be willing. That’s just the cost of doing business in journalism and that’ll happen and you just can’t think about it. We are trying to be grown up and fair.

sentences.en: We do obviously write stories that they don’t like all the time.
sentences.zh: 显然我们总是写他们不喜欢的故事。

sentences.en: We try really, really hard to be fair.
sentences.zh: 我们非常非常努力地做到公平。

sentences.en: We try not to sandbag people, but there are two different things.
sentences.zh: 我们尽量不让人们陷入沙袋，但有两件不同的事情。

sentences.en: One is, “Did you write a story that upset them and they canceled on you?”
sentences.zh: 一是，“你是否写了一个让他们不高兴的故事，然后他们取消了你的计划？”

sentences.en: You just have to be willing.
sentences.zh: 你只需要愿意。

sentences.en: That’s just the cost of doing business in journalism and that’ll happen and you just can’t think about it.
sentences.zh: 这只是新闻业的经营成本，这种情况将会发生，而你根本无法想象。

sentences.en: We are trying to be grown up and fair.
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力变得成熟和公平。

blocks.html_en: One of the things that I’ve noticed is there’s a sense, particularly if you go to these conferences that are not run by journalists, that you don’t want to ask the hard question. You’re a little nervous about there being this core question in the CEO’s business or in this politician’s leadership that is awkward to ask. But of course that’s the question that the CEO spends all his or her time thinking about. Not only are they ready for it, they’ve also thought about it more than anybody else. They’re eager to engage on it.

sentences.en: One of the things that I’ve noticed is there’s a sense, particularly if you go to these conferences that are not run by journalists, that you don’t want to ask the hard question.
sentences.zh: 我注意到的一件事是，有一种感觉，特别是如果你参加这些不是由记者主持的会议，你不想问棘手的问题。

sentences.en: You’re a little nervous about there being this core question in the CEO’s business or in this politician’s leadership that is awkward to ask.
sentences.zh: 你对首席执行官的业务或政客的领导力中存在这个难以提出的核心问题感到有点紧张。

sentences.en: But of course that’s the question that the CEO spends all his or her time thinking about.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是首席执行官花费所有时间思考的问题。

sentences.en: Not only are they ready for it, they’ve also thought about it more than anybody else.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅为此做好了准备，而且比任何人都考虑得更多。

sentences.en: They’re eager to engage on it.
sentences.zh: 他们渴望参与其中。

blocks.html_en: It’s like a weird illusion that senior leaders don’t want to be asked hard questions. That’s crazy. The reason they’re in those gigs is because they find it really interesting. They’re much more relaxing jobs.

sentences.en: It’s like a weird illusion that senior leaders don’t want to be asked hard questions.
sentences.zh: 这就像一种奇怪的错觉，认为高层领导不想被问到尖锐的问题。

sentences.en: That’s crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: The reason they’re in those gigs is because they find it really interesting.
sentences.zh: 他们参加这些演出的原因是因为他们觉得这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: They’re much more relaxing jobs.
sentences.zh: 它们是更轻松的工作。

blocks.html_en: If you’re interviewing the CEO of Ford and you’re not asking him — and how are you not? — about this crisis of China swallowing their business, what are you doing? There is an impulse, which I think is totally wrong, to tiptoe around the hard questions. I actually think for CEOs, for political leaders, it’s boring for them to go on stage and tell the same canned anecdotes about their personal biographies they’ve told a thousand times. It’s their job to answer hard questions.

sentences.en: If you’re interviewing the CEO of Ford and you’re not asking him — and how are you not? — about this crisis of China swallowing their business, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 如果你正在采访福特首席执行官并且你没有问他——你怎么不问他呢？ ——关于中国吞噬他们业务的这场危机，你在做什么？

sentences.en: There is an impulse, which I think is totally wrong, to tiptoe around the hard questions.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种小心翼翼地回避难题的冲动，我认为这是完全错误的。

sentences.en: I actually think for CEOs, for political leaders, it’s boring for them to go on stage and tell the same canned anecdotes about their personal biographies they’ve told a thousand times.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为对于首席执行官和政治领导人来说，他们上台讲述他们已经讲过一千遍的关于他们个人传记的同样的罐头轶事是很无聊的。

sentences.en: It’s their job to answer hard questions.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作就是回答难题。

blocks.html_en: I’m always asked by various comms people, “Why do the CEOs come on the show?” In our YouTube comments, people ask, “Why would they show up?” The answer I’ve most commonly gotten is this is the only way their own employees will listen to them.

sentences.en: I’m always asked by various comms people, “Why do the CEOs come on the show?”
sentences.zh: 各种传播人士总是问我：“为什么首席执行官们要来参加这个节目？”

sentences.en: In our YouTube comments, people ask, “Why would they show up?”
sentences.zh: 在我们的 YouTube 评论中，人们会问：“他们为什么会出现？”

sentences.en: The answer I’ve most commonly gotten is this is the only way their own employees will listen to them.
sentences.zh: 我最常得到的答案是，这是他们自己的员工倾听他们意见的唯一方式。

blocks.html_en: They want to see the challenge and the stakes and the conflict as you’ve described are present in this format, whereas no one’s listening to the all-hands.

sentences.en: They want to see the challenge and the stakes and the conflict as you’ve described are present in this format, whereas no one’s listening to the all-hands.
sentences.zh: 他们希望看到你所描述的挑战、利害关系和冲突以这种形式出现，而没有人倾听全体成员的意见。

blocks.html_en: It’s important that you be respectful. There’s a slice of tech journalism that really concluded that the people they cover are monsters. It’s probably hard to get those folks to talk to you then. Conversely, there’s a slice of the tech industry that has concluded all journalists are in a deep conspiracy to destroy them.

sentences.en: It’s important that you be respectful.
sentences.zh: 保持尊重很重要。

sentences.en: There’s a slice of tech journalism that really concluded that the people they cover are monsters.
sentences.zh: 有一部分科技新闻确实得出了这样的结论：他们报道的人都是怪物。

sentences.en: It’s probably hard to get those folks to talk to you then.
sentences.zh: 那时可能很难让那些人跟你说话。

sentences.en: Conversely, there’s a slice of the tech industry that has concluded all journalists are in a deep conspiracy to destroy them.
sentences.zh: 相反，科技行业的一部分人得出的结论是，所有记者都在密谋摧毁他们。

blocks.html_en: Both of those slices of media culture have run their course and are both toxic and boring at this point. Everybody should stop and just cover these people like important decision makers in the middle of great stories. That’s just the news business.

sentences.en: Both of those slices of media culture have run their course and are both toxic and boring at this point.
sentences.zh: 这两种媒体文化都已经走到了尽头，在这一点上既有毒又无聊。

sentences.en: Everybody should stop and just cover these people like important decision makers in the middle of great stories.
sentences.zh: 每个人都应该停下来，像报道伟大故事中的重要决策者一样报道这些人。

sentences.en: That’s just the news business.
sentences.zh: 这只是新闻业务。

blocks.html_en: We care a lot about our independence and other journalists’ independence and build it deeply into the events.

sentences.en: We care a lot about our independence and other journalists’ independence and build it deeply into the events.
sentences.zh: 我们非常关心我们和其他记者的独立性，并将其深深融入到活动中。

blocks.html_en: It’s more than a slice on either side. Our own audience says, “All of these people are monsters,” and they’re reading a tech website. I look at most of the politicians in America. They’ve come around to, “Maybe we should stop the data centers, or we should at least talk about it because people will like us if we talk about it.” After a decade of talking about regulating social media—

sentences.en: It’s more than a slice on either side.
sentences.zh: 两边都不仅仅是一片。

sentences.en: Our own audience says, “All of these people are monsters,” and they’re reading a tech website.
sentences.zh: 我们自己的观众说，“所有这些人都是怪物”，他们正在阅读一个科技网站。

sentences.en: I look at most of the politicians in America.
sentences.zh: 我观察了美国的大多数政客。

sentences.en: They’ve come around to, “Maybe we should stop the data centers, or we should at least talk about it because people will like us if we talk about it.”
sentences.zh: 他们开始意识到，“也许我们应该停止数据中心，或者我们至少应该谈论它，因为如果我们谈论它，人们会喜欢我们。”

sentences.en: After a decade of talking about regulating social media—
sentences.zh: 经过十年关于监管社交媒体的讨论——

blocks.html_en: And not doing it.

sentences.en: And not doing it.
sentences.zh: 并且不这样做。

blocks.html_en: —and clamping down on Big Tech and doing nothing, we’ve never passed a privacy law in this country.

sentences.en: —and clamping down on Big Tech and doing nothing, we’ve never passed a privacy law in this country.
sentences.zh: -并且压制大型科技公司却无所作为，我们从未在这个国家通过隐私法。

blocks.html_en: You see there’s a lot of heat around “these guys are monsters, we can just throw sticks and stones at them.” And then on the other side, they own the distribution channels. They’re on X, doing whatever they want to do. There’s a sense that they don’t need the accountability.

sentences.en: You see there’s a lot of heat around “these guys are monsters, we can just throw sticks and stones at them.”
sentences.zh: 你看，“这些家伙是怪物，我们可以向他们扔棍子和石头。”

sentences.en: And then on the other side, they own the distribution channels.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他们拥有分销渠道。

sentences.en: They’re on X, doing whatever they want to do.
sentences.zh: 他们在X上，做任何他们想做的事。

sentences.en: There’s a sense that they don’t need the accountability.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，他们不需要责任。

blocks.html_en: Mark Zuckerberg just published a 6,500 word manifesto that in my estimation is freshman year political science thinking. He’s going to get away with it because there’s literally no one around him to say, “Try being smarter than this.”

sentences.en: Mark Zuckerberg just published a 6,500 word manifesto that in my estimation is freshman year political science thinking.
sentences.zh: 马克·扎克伯格刚刚发表了一份 6,500 字的宣言，我认为这是大一时的政治科学思考。

sentences.en: He’s going to get away with it because there’s literally no one around him to say, “Try being smarter than this.”
sentences.zh: 他会侥幸逃脱惩罚，因为他周围几乎没有人会说：“试着变得比这更聪明。”

blocks.html_en: Do you see that connection at your events, where the thing you need to challenge some of these executives on is people think you have bad values, not your business decisions?

sentences.en: Do you see that connection at your events, where the thing you need to challenge some of these executives on is people think you have bad values, not your business decisions?
sentences.zh: 您是否在您的活动中看到了这种联系，您需要挑战其中一些高管的事情是人们认为您的价值观不好，而不是您的业务决策？

blocks.html_en: When you are interviewing somebody where there’s a core critique of the thing they’re doing that is the values, you should definitely ask. You always ask them. That’s the question they’ve been thinking about, too.

sentences.en: When you are interviewing somebody where there’s a core critique of the thing they’re doing that is the values, you should definitely ask.
sentences.zh: 当你采访某人时，如果有人对他们正在做的事情提出核心批评，那就是价值观，你一定要问。

sentences.en: You always ask them.
sentences.zh: 你总是问他们。

sentences.en: That’s the question they’ve been thinking about, too.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们一直在思考的问题。

blocks.html_en: I actually disagree with you on the AI CEOs though. We’re moving out of an era where you had business leaders. Marc Andreessen is patient zero of this — very, very smart guy, very influential and influenced a lot of people to think this way, but who had this deep paranoia about the media and the sense that it wasn’t relevant.

sentences.en: I actually disagree with you on the AI CEOs though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我实际上不同意你对人工智能首席执行官的看法。

sentences.en: We’re moving out of an era where you had business leaders.
sentences.zh: 我们正在走出一个拥有商业领袖的时代。

sentences.en: Marc Andreessen is patient zero of this — very, very smart guy, very influential and influenced a lot of people to think this way, but who had this deep paranoia about the media and the sense that it wasn’t relevant.
sentences.zh: 马克·安德森（Marc Andreessen）是这方面的零号病人——非常非常聪明的人，非常有影响力，影响了很多人以这种方式思考，但他对媒体有一种深深的偏执，觉得它不相关。

blocks.html_en: If you look at the really great business figures of this era, of the new ones — I would say Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Jensen Huang — these are classic showmen who love the media. Or I don’t know if they love the media or they hate the media, but they, like Steve Jobs, understand it, like Donald Trump.

sentences.en: If you look at the really great business figures of this era, of the new ones — I would say Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Jensen Huang — these are classic showmen who love the media.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看这个时代真正伟大的商业人物，或者新的商业人物——我会说达里奥·阿莫迪、山姆·奥尔特曼和黄仁勋——他们都是热爱媒体的经典表演者。

sentences.en: Or I don’t know if they love the media or they hate the media, but they, like Steve Jobs, understand it, like Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 或者我不知道他们是喜欢媒体还是讨厌媒体，但他们像史蒂夫·乔布斯一样理解媒体，就像唐纳德·特朗普一样。

blocks.html_en: They’re selling something.

sentences.en: They’re selling something.
sentences.zh: 他们在卖东西。

blocks.html_en: They’re salesmen who see the media as a very important sales channel, which is how business leaders have always been. They’re running circles around the guys and the women who are sitting paranoid, saying, “I don’t know if we can talk to this reporter.”

sentences.en: They’re salesmen who see the media as a very important sales channel, which is how business leaders have always been.
sentences.zh: 他们是销售人员，将媒体视为非常重要的销售渠道，这也是企业领导者一直以来的态度。

sentences.en: They’re running circles around the guys and the women who are sitting paranoid, saying, “I don’t know if we can talk to this reporter.”
sentences.zh: 他们在那些偏执的男人和女人周围跑来跑去，说：“我不知道我们是否可以和这位记者谈谈。”

blocks.html_en: They just pick up the phone and they’re on the cover and they wear the leather jacket and they do whatever the slightly corny but incredibly effective Time magazine cover style thing is. Obviously the legacy media is diminished and there are new outlets, but fundamentally they’re showmen who aren’t operating out of some kind of deep theoretical relationship with media that they plan to change.

sentences.en: They just pick up the phone and they’re on the cover and they wear the leather jacket and they do whatever the slightly corny but incredibly effective Time magazine cover style thing is.
sentences.zh: 他们只要拿起电话，就登上封面，穿着皮夹克，做任何有点老套但非常有效的《时代》杂志封面风格的事情。

sentences.en: Obviously the legacy media is diminished and there are new outlets, but fundamentally they’re showmen who aren’t operating out of some kind of deep theoretical relationship with media that they plan to change.
sentences.zh: 显然，传统媒体正在减少，并且出现了新的渠道，但从根本上来说，他们只是表演者，他们并没有与他们计划改变的媒体建立某种深厚的理论关系。

blocks.html_en: Elon is obviously the big exception to this rule, as of many, but the rest of this new generation of business leaders have a much more normal relationship with the media.

sentences.en: Elon is obviously the big exception to this rule, as of many, but the rest of this new generation of business leaders have a much more normal relationship with the media.
sentences.zh: 和许多人一样，埃隆显然是这条规则的一个大例外，但新一代商界领袖的其他人与媒体的关系要正常得多。

blocks.html_en: One of the things that I think is really interesting in that context is the rise of the news creator, the news influencer, where they aren’t of the machine the way that you are of the machine. They don’t have a Justin Smith saying, “I’ve built a global news operation. You just do the great reporting, I’ll find new business. By the way, all the big print newspapers have task forces. We will have a global conference and solve independence.”

sentences.en: One of the things that I think is really interesting in that context is the rise of the news creator, the news influencer, where they aren’t of the machine the way that you are of the machine.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这种背景下真正有趣的事情之一是新闻创造者、新闻影响者的崛起，他们不像你那样属于机器。

sentences.en: They don’t have a Justin Smith saying, “I’ve built a global news operation.
sentences.zh: 他们没有像贾斯汀·史密斯那样说：“我建立了一个全球新闻机构。

sentences.en: You just do the great reporting, I’ll find new business.
sentences.zh: 你只要做出色的报道，我就会找到新的业务。

sentences.en: By the way, all the big print newspapers have task forces.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，所有大印刷报纸都有特别工作组。

sentences.en: We will have a global conference and solve independence.”
sentences.zh: 我们将召开一次全球会议并解决独立问题。”

blocks.html_en: The influencers and creators I talk to, this is all a first impression for them. The idea that they can be plied with gifts or access or made to seem more important, they feel it.

sentences.en: The influencers and creators I talk to, this is all a first impression for them.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的影响者和创作者，这都是他们的第一印象。

sentences.en: The idea that they can be plied with gifts or access or made to seem more important, they feel it.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉到，他们可以得到礼物或机会，或者让自己看起来更重要。

blocks.html_en: They struggle with it on a deep level. A lot of our industrialists and politicians now understand that that is a faster route to a bigger audience and that there’s more influence to be had there over the content, over the editorial. How do you compete with that?

sentences.en: They struggle with it on a deep level.
sentences.zh: 他们在深层次上与之斗争。

sentences.en: A lot of our industrialists and politicians now understand that that is a faster route to a bigger audience and that there’s more influence to be had there over the content, over the editorial.
sentences.zh: 我们的许多实业家和政治家现在都明白，这是获得更多受众的更快途径，而且对内容和社论的影响力更大。

sentences.en: How do you compete with that?
sentences.zh: 你如何与之竞争？

blocks.html_en: You have to have courage in your conviction that people want journalism, that people actually would like true facts rather than lies and independent voices rather than ones that are corrupt. That’s a very optimistic view, but that’s broadly true. You’re seeing that the most interesting and most successful creators are also finding that.

sentences.en: You have to have courage in your conviction that people want journalism, that people actually would like true facts rather than lies and independent voices rather than ones that are corrupt.
sentences.zh: 你必须有勇气相信人们想要新闻业，人们实际上喜欢真实的事实而不是谎言，喜欢独立的声音而不是腐败的声音。

sentences.en: That’s a very optimistic view, but that’s broadly true.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常乐观的观点，但大体上是正确的。

sentences.en: You’re seeing that the most interesting and most successful creators are also finding that.
sentences.zh: 你会看到最有趣、最成功的创作者也发现了这一点。

blocks.html_en: The great Silicon Valley podcaster Dwarkesh Patel’s questions have gotten tougher and tougher because he’s very sophisticated and I think he realizes his audience knows that, if you’re interviewing Jensen Huang about how he thinks about chips in China, you should ask him the hard questions, not the easy ones, and that’s more interesting. It’s so obvious. For journalists who admire or worry about creators, there’s some lacking in the courage of their own convictions that it is more interesting to ask hard questions than easy ones.

sentences.en: The great Silicon Valley podcaster Dwarkesh Patel’s questions have gotten tougher and tougher because he’s very sophisticated and I think he realizes his audience knows that, if you’re interviewing Jensen Huang about how he thinks about chips in China, you should ask him the hard questions, not the easy ones, and that’s more interesting.
sentences.zh: 伟大的硅谷播客 Dwarkesh Patel 的问题变得越来越棘手，因为他非常老练，我认为他意识到他的观众知道，如果你采访黄仁勋关于他如何看待中国的芯片，你应该问他困难的问题，而不是简单的问题，这更有趣。

sentences.en: It’s so obvious.
sentences.zh: 太明显了。

sentences.en: For journalists who admire or worry about creators, there’s some lacking in the courage of their own convictions that it is more interesting to ask hard questions than easy ones.
sentences.zh: 对于那些钦佩或担心创作者的记者来说，有些人缺乏勇气，坚信提出困难的问题比简单的问题更有趣。

blocks.html_en: Don’t you need the person to show up to be asked the questions of? This is the dynamic that I see in so many places. With the podcasters and the creators, what they’re learning is that their audiences are durable. You don’t need the famous person. You don’t need Apple access to get your big audience. If you have a big audience, you can do whatever you want. My formulation of that is the less access you need, the more you get. But that’s a hard lesson to learn at the beginning.

sentences.en: Don’t you need the person to show up to be asked the questions of?
sentences.zh: 你不需要那个人出现来接受提问吗？

sentences.en: This is the dynamic that I see in so many places.
sentences.zh: 这就是我在很多地方看到的动态。

sentences.en: With the podcasters and the creators, what they’re learning is that their audiences are durable.
sentences.zh: 对于播客和创作者来说，他们学到的是他们的观众是持久的。

sentences.en: You don’t need the famous person.
sentences.zh: 你不需要名人。

sentences.en: You don’t need Apple access to get your big audience.
sentences.zh: 您不需要 Apple 访问权限即可吸引大量受众。

sentences.en: If you have a big audience, you can do whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你有很多观众，你就可以做任何你想做的事。

sentences.en: My formulation of that is the less access you need, the more you get.
sentences.zh: 我的表述是，您需要的访问权限越少，获得的权限就越多。

sentences.en: But that’s a hard lesson to learn at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 但这是一开始就很难学到的教训。

blocks.html_en: There’s an old saying that access is a curse, too.

sentences.en: There’s an old saying that access is a curse, too.
sentences.zh: 有句老话说，访问也是一种诅咒。

blocks.html_en: Oh, access is poisonous.

sentences.en: Oh, access is poisonous.
sentences.zh: 哦，访问是有毒的。

blocks.html_en: I follow politics very closely, and you see this in Washington. I don’t know if you remember, but in the beginning of the Trump administration, there were all these influencers in the White House press conferences asking Karoline Leavitt how she does her hair. The thing is I think they and their audiences found that that was extremely boring, and they wandered off to talk instead about having paranoid fights with Candace Owens or whatever.

sentences.en: I follow politics very closely, and you see this in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我非常密切地关注政治，你在华盛顿也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: I don’t know if you remember, but in the beginning of the Trump administration, there were all these influencers in the White House press conferences asking Karoline Leavitt how she does her hair.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否还记得，在特朗普执政之初，白宫新闻发布会上所有这些有影响力的人物都询问卡罗琳·莱维特如何打理头发。

sentences.en: The thing is I think they and their audiences found that that was extremely boring, and they wandered off to talk instead about having paranoid fights with Candace Owens or whatever.
sentences.zh: 问题是，我认为他们和他们的观众发现这非常无聊，他们就走开去谈论与坎迪斯·欧文斯或其他人进行偏执的战斗。

blocks.html_en: Similarly, the Pentagon in particular brought in all these what they saw as allied, pliable, right-wing influencers to replace the hated mainstream media. And then when the Iran war started, Gateway Pundit is grilling Pete Hegseth about the war and he doesn’t have answers because there are a lot of toxic things about audience capture and you can be pulled all sorts of crazy places by your audience, but also you can be pulled toward journalism by your audience.

sentences.en: Similarly, the Pentagon in particular brought in all these what they saw as allied, pliable, right-wing influencers to replace the hated mainstream media.
sentences.zh: 同样，五角大楼特别引入了所有他们认为是盟友、灵活的右翼影响者来取代令人讨厌的主流媒体。

sentences.en: And then when the Iran war started, Gateway Pundit is grilling Pete Hegseth about the war and he doesn’t have answers because there are a lot of toxic things about audience capture and you can be pulled all sorts of crazy places by your audience, but also you can be pulled toward journalism by your audience.
sentences.zh: 然后当伊朗战争开始时，Gateway Pundit 就战争问题盘问 Pete Hegseth，他没有答案，因为吸引观众有很多有毒的东西，你可能会被你的观众拉到各种疯狂的地方，但你也可能会被你的观众拉向新闻业。

blocks.html_en: What you saw in that Pentagon press room was that their audiences were nervous about the war and did not like it. So suddenly Pete Hegseth is being grilled by these pet outlets that he’d put in there to avoid dealing with real questions. There was some sense that journalism isn’t a trade that you learned at journalism school. It is actually a service to your audience that anybody can figure out if you are paying attention.

sentences.en: What you saw in that Pentagon press room was that their audiences were nervous about the war and did not like it.
sentences.zh: 你在五角大楼新闻发布室看到的是，他们的观众对战争感到紧张并且不喜欢它。

sentences.en: So suddenly Pete Hegseth is being grilled by these pet outlets that he’d put in there to avoid dealing with real questions.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 遭到了这些宠物店的盘问，他之所以把这些宠物店放在那里是为了避免处理真正的问题。

sentences.en: There was some sense that journalism isn’t a trade that you learned at journalism school.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，新闻业并不是你在新闻学校学到的一门职业。

sentences.en: It is actually a service to your audience that anybody can figure out if you are paying attention.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是为你的观众提供的一项服务，任何人都可以知道你是否在关注。

blocks.html_en: One of the really interesting things to me about that dynamic in particular at the Pentagon is so many of the journalists they put in there were video first. They were making clips. I could see them in those press conferences trying to get a clip. They knew the video would play and then the platforms reward conflict, and the comments were, “Why did you ask this question?”

sentences.en: One of the really interesting things to me about that dynamic in particular at the Pentagon is so many of the journalists they put in there were video first.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，关于这种动态的真正有趣的事情之一，特别是在五角大楼，他们派驻在那里的许多记者首先是视频。

sentences.en: They were making clips.
sentences.zh: 他们正在制作剪辑。

sentences.en: I could see them in those press conferences trying to get a clip.
sentences.zh: 我可以在新闻发布会上看到他们试图获取剪辑。

sentences.en: They knew the video would play and then the platforms reward conflict, and the comments were, “Why did you ask this question?”
sentences.zh: 他们知道视频会播放，然后平台会奖励冲突，评论是：“你为什么问这个问题？”

blocks.html_en: What do you think Sam Donaldson was doing in the White House press room in the 1980s? These are stages for performance.

sentences.en: What do you think Sam Donaldson was doing in the White House press room in the 1980s?
sentences.zh: 您认为 20 世纪 80 年代萨姆·唐纳森 (Sam Donaldson) 在白宫新闻发布室做什么？

sentences.en: These are stages for performance.

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Who was it?
sentences.zh: 是谁？

sentences.en: It was Newt Gingrich who figured out C-SPAN was the stage for him.
sentences.zh: Newt Gingrich 发现 C-SPAN 是他的舞台。

sentences.en: I understand, but the clip economy in particular.
sentences.zh: 我理解，但尤其是剪辑经济。

blocks.html_en: They’re going to manufacture a clip, and maybe it’s the audience pulling you towards journalism or maybe it’s just the algorithm pulling you towards conflict.

sentences.en: They’re going to manufacture a clip, and maybe it’s the audience pulling you towards journalism or maybe it’s just the algorithm pulling you towards conflict.
sentences.zh: 他们要制作一个剪辑，也许是观众把你拉向新闻业，或者也许只是算法把你拉向冲突。

sentences.en: There are good pulls and there are bad pulls, for sure.
sentences.zh: 当然，有好的拉力，也有坏的拉力。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes it’s hard to tell the difference. You’re doing more video now, and that’s right next to the fact that the Semaform is there to expose the structure of journalism because its audience is really smart and some of them are CEOs. sentences.en: Sometimes it’s hard to tell the difference.
sentences.zh: 有时很难区分。

sentences.en: You’re doing more video now, and that’s right next to the fact that the Semaform is there to expose the structure of journalism because its audience is really smart and some of them are CEOs.
sentences.zh: 你现在正在制作更多的视频，而这正是 Semaform 的目的是揭露新闻业的结构，因为它的观众非常聪明，其中一些是首席执行官。

sentences.en: And then you’re going to go make video on video platforms and you’re going to experience that other pull.
sentences.zh: 然后你将去视频平台上制作视频，你将体验到其他的吸引力。

sentences.en: How do you think about managing that?
sentences.zh: 您如何看待管理这个问题？

sentences.en: Are you not chasing scale?
sentences.zh: 你不追求规模吗？

blocks.html_en: No, we think about it a lot, about not chasing scale on video, but trying to have really high-level conversations. That there’s a big — but not the biggest — audience for really sophisticated conversations with leaders in media or in Compound Interest, our business show; CEOs on our CEO Signal show; and other stuff we’re going to be launching.

sentences.en: No, we think about it a lot, about not chasing scale on video, but trying to have really high-level conversations.
sentences.zh: 不，我们想了很多，关于不追求视频的规模，而是尝试进行真正的高层对话。

sentences.en: That there’s a big — but not the biggest — audience for really sophisticated conversations with leaders in media or in Compound Interest, our business show; CEOs on our CEO Signal show; and other stuff we’re going to be launching.
sentences.zh: 在媒体或我们的商业节目《复利》中，有大量（但不是最大的）观众愿意与领导者进行真正复杂的对话；我们的首席执行官信号节目中的首席执行官；以及我们将要推出的其他东西。

blocks.html_en: Video reminds me so much of the social web, and the allure of infinite scale if you just follow it toward this fixed point that everyone else is also going toward. sentences.en: Video reminds me so much of the social web, and the allure of infinite scale if you just follow it toward this fixed point that everyone else is also going toward.
sentences.zh: 视频让我想起了社交网络，以及如果你跟随它走向其他人也在走向的固定点，就会感受到无限规模的诱惑。

sentences.en: It’s this incredibly homogenizing force.
sentences.zh: 这就是令人难以置信的同质化力量。

sentences.en: Everybody on the left is doing Bari Weiss outrage this week, and it’s very, very hyper partisan.
sentences.zh: 本周，左翼人士都对巴里·韦斯表示愤怒，而且党派之争非常非常强烈。

sentences.en: No, we just have really had a lot of internal conversations about resisting that.
sentences.zh: 不，我们只是进行了很多关于抵制这种行为的内部对话。

blocks.html_en: How do you make money if you don’t chase scale on video?

sentences.en: How do you make money if you don’t chase scale on video?
sentences.zh: 如果你不追求视频规模，你如何赚钱？

blocks.html_en: You have to reach a really high-quality audience.

sentences.en: You have to reach a really high-quality audience.
sentences.zh: 你必须接触到真正高质量的受众。

blocks.html_en: And you’re just going to bake the ads in? Are you going to do the ad reads? This is the other big problem of the creator world is the platforms don’t pay you any money, and they’ve certainly learned to pay people less money.

sentences.en: And you’re just going to bake the ads in?
sentences.zh: 你只是要把广告放进去吗？

sentences.en: Are you going to do the ad reads?
sentences.zh: 你要读广告吗？

sentences.en: This is the other big problem of the creator world is the platforms don’t pay you any money, and they’ve certainly learned to pay people less money.
sentences.zh: 这是创作者世界的另一个大问题，平台不会付给你任何钱，而且他们当然已经学会了付给人们更少的钱。

blocks.html_en: Yes, we do integrated campaigns with direct-sold advertisers. I don’t know. You do host reads. I noticed that Odd Lots, my second favorite show, is doing host reads these days.

sentences.en: Yes, we do integrated campaigns with direct-sold advertisers.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们与直销广告商进行整合营销活动。

sentences.en: I don’t know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: You do host reads.
sentences.zh: 你做主持人阅读。

sentences.en: I noticed that Odd Lots, my second favorite show, is doing host reads these days.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我第二喜欢的节目《Odd Lot》最近正在做主持人阅读。

blocks.html_en: This is the biggest concept in all of media.

sentences.en: This is the biggest concept in all of media.
sentences.zh: 这是所有媒体中最大的概念。

blocks.html_en: The principle of journalistic independence is incredibly important. The forms change when you’re in these moments. What I remember is that on Google, the ads used to be in yellow and they had a yellow overlay. At BuzzFeed, we said, “Okay, that’s the convention. We’ll have a yellow overlay on our ads. That’s how you know it’s an ad.”

sentences.en: The principle of journalistic independence is incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 新闻独立性原则非常重要。

sentences.en: The forms change when you’re in these moments.
sentences.zh: 当你处于这些时刻时，形式就会改变。

sentences.en: What I remember is that on Google, the ads used to be in yellow and they had a yellow overlay.
sentences.zh: 我记得在谷歌上，广告曾经是黄色的，并且有黄色的覆盖层。

sentences.en: At BuzzFeed, we said, “Okay, that’s the convention.
sentences.zh: 在 BuzzFeed，我们说：“好吧，这就是惯例。

sentences.en: We’ll have a yellow overlay on our ads.
sentences.zh: 我们的广告上会有黄色叠加层。

sentences.en: That’s how you know it’s an ad.”
sentences.zh: 这样你就知道这是广告。”

blocks.html_en: Then Google removed it, and we said, “I guess that’s not the convention. I guess ads can be the same color as everything else.” These things are signals to the audience and the forms change through time. Again, you don’t want to be innovating the field of ethics, but you have to realize that the forms are changing.

sentences.en: Then Google removed it, and we said, “I guess that’s not the convention.
sentences.zh: 然后谷歌删除了它，我们说，“我想这不是惯例。

sentences.en: I guess ads can be the same color as everything else.”
sentences.zh: 我想广告可以和其他东西的颜色一样。”

sentences.en: These things are signals to the audience and the forms change through time.
sentences.zh: 这些东西是向观众发出的信号，形式会随着时间而变化。

sentences.en: Again, you don’t want to be innovating the field of ethics, but you have to realize that the forms are changing.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，你不想在道德领域进行创新，但你必须意识到形式正在发生变化。

blocks.html_en: My harshest take about all these platforms is Google made the ads not yellow and then it made them look like the content, and then it changed the economics of the web such that the only profitable thing to publish on the web is marketing content and listicles about what shoes to buy when you go hiking, and now that’s all that shows up in AI Overviews.

sentences.en: My harshest take about all these platforms is Google made the ads not yellow and then it made them look like the content, and then it changed the economics of the web such that the only profitable thing to publish on the web is marketing content and listicles about what shoes to buy when you go hiking, and now that’s all that shows up in AI Overviews.
sentences.zh: 我对所有这些平台最严厉的看法是，谷歌让广告不是黄色的，然后让它们看起来像内容，然后它改变了网络的经济学，使得在网络上发布的唯一有利可图的东西是营销内容和关于徒步旅行时要买什么鞋子的列表，现在这就是人工智能概述中显示的全部内容。

blocks.html_en: And then Meta started charging you to distribute those rather than letting them go viral on their own if they were good.

sentences.en: And then Meta started charging you to distribute those rather than letting them go viral on their own if they were good.
sentences.zh: 然后 Meta 开始向你收取分发这些内容的费用，而不是让它们自行传播（如果它们很好的话）。

blocks.html_en: So everything became advertising. YouTube just made it harder to make money on YouTube. They changed the rules of their partner program. The only way you can make real money as a creator on YouTube and have your big staff is if you do the integrated brand campaign — if you become an advertiser or an ad agency.

sentences.en: So everything became advertising.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都变成了广告。

sentences.en: YouTube just made it harder to make money on YouTube.
sentences.zh: YouTube 只是让在 YouTube 上赚钱变得更加困难。

sentences.en: They changed the rules of their partner program.
sentences.zh: 他们改变了合作伙伴计划的规则。

sentences.en: The only way you can make real money as a creator on YouTube and have your big staff is if you do the integrated brand campaign — if you become an advertiser or an ad agency.
sentences.zh: 作为 YouTube 上的创作者，您能够真正赚钱并拥有大量员工的唯一方法是进行整合的品牌活动 - 如果您成为广告商或广告代理商。

blocks.html_en: That is the pull of all these platforms: “We’re not going to pay you anything, we’re going to take the content for free, maybe we’ll even train our AI on it, and you will integrate advertising it somewhere.” I get what you’re saying about not innovating in ethics, but as someone who has resisted the many, many, many demands that I do the host reads and the checks that come along with it, that’s the innovation is we’re making the reporters read the ads now.

sentences.en: That is the pull of all these platforms: “We’re not going to pay you anything, we’re going to take the content for free, maybe we’ll even train our AI on it, and you will integrate advertising it somewhere.”
sentences.zh: 这就是所有这些平台的吸引力：“我们不会向你支付任何费用，我们将免费获取内容，也许我们甚至会在上面训练我们的人工智能，然后你将在某个地方整合广告。”

sentences.en: I get what you’re saying about not innovating in ethics, but as someone who has resisted the many, many, many demands that I do the host reads and the checks that come along with it, that’s the innovation is we’re making the reporters read the ads now.
sentences.zh: 我明白你所说的道德上没有创新，但作为一个拒绝了我提出的许多、许多、许多要求的人，主持人阅读并随之而来的检查，这就是创新，我们现在让记者阅读广告。

blocks.html_en: In the old days of TV and radio, the hosts read the ads, and then they stopped. Now they do it again. Maybe there’s some study saying they were more corrupt. But I haven’t really seen any evidence of that. I just think these are different kinds of forms.

sentences.en: In the old days of TV and radio, the hosts read the ads, and then they stopped.
sentences.zh: 在过去的电视和广播中，主持人读了广告，然后就停止了。

sentences.en: Now they do it again.
sentences.zh: 现在他们又这么做了。

sentences.en: Maybe there’s some study saying they were more corrupt.
sentences.zh: 也许有一些研究表明他们更腐败。

sentences.en: But I haven’t really seen any evidence of that.
sentences.zh: 但我还没有真正看到任何证据。

sentences.en: I just think these are different kinds of forms.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为这些是不同类型的形式。

blocks.html_en: It used to be that front page advertising in newspapers was considered horrifically corrupt and now they do it all the time. sentences.en: It used to be that front page advertising in newspapers was considered horrifically corrupt and now they do it all the time.
sentences.zh: 过去，报纸头版广告被认为是极其腐败的行为，而现在他们却一直这样做。

sentences.en: Some of this stuff is people get caught up on the forms in a medium that’s just changing really, really fast.
sentences.zh: 其中一些事情是人们沉迷于变化非常非常快的媒介中的形式。

sentences.en: No, we want to create amazing advertising that our advertisers are really happy with and works for them.
sentences.zh: 不，我们希望制作令人惊叹的广告，让我们的广告商真正满意并为他们服务。

sentences.en: That’s just core to the business.
sentences.zh: 这只是业务的核心。

sentences.en: It is another nice thing about starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 从头开始是另一件好事。

blocks.html_en: There’s a difference between when you’re building a media company, as you have done, thinking about, “This is a product that our audience is going to love and that our advertisers are going to love.” And in that neonatal state, church and state can talk to each other a lot. sentences.en: There’s a difference between when you’re building a media company, as you have done, thinking about, “This is a product that our audience is going to love and that our advertisers are going to love.”
sentences.zh: 当你建立一家媒体公司时，就像你所做的那样，想着“这是我们的观众会喜欢的产品，我们的广告商也会喜欢的产品”，这是有区别的。

sentences.en: And in that neonatal state, church and state can talk to each other a lot.
sentences.zh: 在那个新生的状态下，教会和国家可以互相交谈很多。

sentences.en: Once you launch the thing, they’ve got to be really independent.
sentences.zh: 一旦你推出了这个东西，他们就必须真正独立。

blocks.html_en: This is the core challenge of our time, especially if you want to make something that gets wide distribution. sentences.en: This is the core challenge of our time, especially if you want to make something that gets wide distribution.
sentences.zh: 这是我们这个时代的核心挑战，特别是如果你想制作一些能够广泛传播的东西。

sentences.en: If you want to start a newsletter on Substack or Ghost or Beehiiv and charge a lot of money to a small audience, I think you can do pretty well.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在 Substack、Ghost 或 Beehiiv 上开始发布时事通讯，并向一小部分受众收取大量费用，我认为你可以做得很好。

sentences.en: Your ability to have a massive impact gets immediately limited, as you’ve said.
sentences.zh: 正如您所说，您产生巨大影响的能力立即受到限制。

sentences.en: That is a way to build a big business without reaching a huge scale is to reach a very, very valuable audience.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在不达到巨大规模的情况下建立大企业的方法，即吸引非常非常有价值的受众。

sentences.en: Again, that’s not the only way to build a media company, you wouldn’t want to be in a world where that was the only kind of media company, but we are totally, totally focused on that.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这不是建立媒体公司的唯一方法，你不会想进入一个只有这种媒体公司的世界，但我们完全、完全专注于这一点。

sentences.en: It is working and it is allowing us to hire great journalists to break stories.
sentences.zh: 它正在发挥作用，让我们能够聘请优秀的记者来报道新闻。

sentences.zh: 其中有一部分是，“嗯，我们认为观众很聪明，他们是精英观众，他们了解结构，他们可能理解詹森加入顾问委员会、顾问委员会加入一群沙特皇室成员所带来的偏见。”

sentences.en: How do you feel about that?

sentences.zh: 不，他们非常清楚我们在做什么。

sentences.en: Do they think that that gets some influence?
sentences.zh: 他们认为这会产生一些影响吗？

sentences.en: Because that’s what the consumer audience definitely believes.
sentences.zh: 因为这是消费者观众肯定相信的。

blocks.html_en: I don’t know what they think, but our promise to them is that it doesn’t, and that we’re covering these people very independently. In fact, a lot of the people on these advisory boards have diametrically opposed interests to one another.

sentences.en: I don’t know what they think, but our promise to them is that it doesn’t, and that we’re covering these people very independently.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们怎么想，但我们向他们承诺，事实并非如此，而且我们正在非常独立地报道这些人。

sentences.en: There’s no journalistic followthrough, not any more than I think being on the DealBook task force influences what you see in The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 没有任何新闻后续行动，就像我认为加入 DealBook 特别工作组对你在《纽约时报》上看到的内容的影响一样。
